items.html: 🕰 The Financial Times reported that Big Tech companies have issued up to $300bn of guarantees backing AI data centres and chips in under a year, recording little of it on their balance sheets, including a $28bn Meta guarantee behind its Hyperion venture with Blue Owl — Secondary write-ups of the FT piece say Hyperion raised $27bn with most of the obligation outside Meta's reported balance sheet, and cite Morgan Stanley's broader estimate of more than $3.1tn of off-balance-sheet commitments across seven cloud and chip companies. items.html: 🕰 White House science adviser Michael Kratsios said on Fox News Sunday that AI companies concerned their technology is unsafe "can just stop it. You don't need someone to force you to do that." — He said the government already has tools when a specific risk appears, citing a case this summer in which it sent a letter over credible cybersecurity evidence and "the model was pulled down until those cybersecurity issues were resolved," and dismissed fears of a "Terminator running on the streets." items.title: Google agreed on 09-21 to report content flagged as child sexual abuse material directly to Indian authorities, breaking from the global practice of routing such reports first through the US-based National Center for Missing & Exploited Children, which then relays them to local law enforcement.
items.html: Google agreed on 09-21 to report content flagged as child sexual abuse material directly to Indian authorities, breaking from the global practice of routing such reports first through the US-based National Center for Missing & Exploited Children, which then relays them to local law enforcement. The move follows a similar move by Meta the week before, after two Indian government sources told Reuters they had pressed Google and Microsoft to report India-related child-abuse content directly, arguing the existing relay delays reports in cases where a child may be in active danger. India is the largest market by users for both Google's YouTube and Meta's Facebook; Meta's own shift followed weeks of friction with the Indian government, including an August apology from Mark Zuckerberg over CSAM spreading on its platforms — the same pressure India's National Commission for Protection of Child Rights and IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw put on Meta's "simple intermediary" claim earlier in September. Dated to its real day, Monday 09-21, not a 09-23 development. (Reuters via Yahoo News)

items.title: The Drug Enforcement Administration proposed on 09-23 to place five tryptamine hallucinogens (4-OH-DiPT, 5-MeO-AMT, 5-MeO-MiPT, 5-MeO-DET and DiPT) in Schedule I, nine days after the FDA's psychedelics hearing; comments are open until 10-23.
items.html: The Drug Enforcement Administration proposed on 09-23 to place five tryptamine hallucinogens (4-OH-DiPT, 5-MeO-AMT, 5-MeO-MiPT, 5-MeO-DET and DiPT) in Schedule I, nine days after the FDA's psychedelics hearing; comments are open until 10-23. It is DEA's second attempt: it withdrew a January 2022 proposal, along with the July 2022 hearing notice that followed it, asked HHS for a fresh evaluation in 2023, and received HHS's recommendation on 04-02, and the notice cites "a cumulative total of 518 encounters" of the five compounds by law enforcement. If finalized, Schedule I controls would apply to anyone who manufactures, distributes, researches or possesses them. One of the five, 4-OH-DiPT, is the active form of luvesilocin, Reunion Neuroscience's postpartum-depression drug that the FDA designated a breakthrough therapy on 02-23, which is the contradiction psychedelic-law advocates quoted by Marijuana Moment are pressing. (Federal Register, Marijuana Moment, Reunion Neuroscience)

items.title: Oregon's Health Authority said on 09-22 it will not adopt rules that would have doubled annual license fees for the state's legal psilocybin businesses and ended veteran and low-income discounts, and will open a new rulemaking, planned to take effect 01-15-2027.
items.html: Oregon's Health Authority said on 09-22 it will not adopt rules that would have doubled annual license fees for the state's legal psilocybin businesses and ended veteran and low-income discounts, and will open a new rulemaking, planned to take effect 01-15-2027. Records released under a public-records request projected a $3.8 million shortfall in the program's current two-year budget without the increase, and $2.9 million to $4.2 million with it depending on how many licensees quit; the authority is weighing a higher tax on psilocybin products, and every speaker at two public hearings opposed the fees. Dated to its real day, 09-22. (Oregon Health Authority bulletin, Oregon Capital Chronicle)

items.title: YouTube chief executive Neal Mohan told CNN on 09-23 that YouTube will not join Meta's multistate youth-harm settlement, saying the platform has "invested in making sure that young people are safe" for a very long time.
items.html: YouTube chief executive Neal Mohan told CNN on 09-23 that YouTube will not join Meta's multistate youth-harm settlement, saying the platform has "invested in making sure that young people are safe" for a very long time. The refusal tests the settlement's design: per CNN, Meta said it would pay out only 70% of the deal unless TikTok and YouTube each agreed to pay around $6 billion and adopt similar changes (time limits, no like counts for teens, third-party oversight), and California Attorney General Rob Bonta has said the states are willing to sue both to get them on board. TikTok has not commented and Bonta's office had not responded to CNN. Mohan spoke at the Made on YouTube event; YouTube and Meta were found liable in a separate March Los Angeles trial and both plan to appeal. (CNN)

items.title: A planned White House executive order that would have let a political board veto individual National Institutes of Health grants is "looking dead," Senator Susan Collins and one person familiar with the decision told STAT on 09-23, after bipartisan pushback.
items.html: A planned White House executive order that would have let a political board veto individual National Institutes of Health grants is "looking dead," Senator Susan Collins and one person familiar with the decision told STAT on 09-23, after bipartisan pushback. Collins, who chairs the Senate appropriations committee, wrote the budget director Russell Vought and NIH Director Jay Bhattacharya on 09-22 urging them not to proceed, and Semafor first reported the order was being tempered. The White House did not respond to STAT's request for comment, so the reversal is reported rather than announced. The draft, discussed at an Oval Office meeting on Friday 09-18, would have added a political sign-off on top of NIH peer review. (STAT)

items.title: New York's Medicaid program will cut its direct autism-therapy (applied behavior analysis) rate a third time in a year, to $9.63 a billing unit from $14.45, a 33% cut effective 10-01 that providers say ends Medicaid ABA for children in the state.
items.html: New York's Medicaid program will cut its direct autism-therapy (applied behavior analysis) rate a third time in a year, to $9.63 a billing unit from $14.45, a 33% cut effective 10-01 that providers say ends Medicaid ABA for children in the state. The state announced the rate on 09-17; with two 12.5% cuts (10-2025 and 04-2026) the cumulative reduction is about 50% from early 2025, and Behavioral Health Business, citing MediRate data, reports it would be the lowest Medicaid ABA rate in the country (West Virginia's $9.90 was the previous floor). The state health department told BHB it remains "committed to ensuring access to high-quality, medically necessary care while managing Medicaid resources effectively"; one provider called it "a death sentence of a rate cut." (Behavioral Health Business)

items.title: A University of Illinois Chicago trial of "Coach Lumen," a voice-based AI coach delivering problem-solving therapy, posted results on ClinicalTrials.gov on 09-23: at 18 weeks, participants coached by the AI improved more than a delayed-treatment control, and those coached by a human improved somewhat more than the AI-coached group on most measures, in unadjusted registry means.
items.html: A University of Illinois Chicago trial of "Coach Lumen," a voice-based AI coach delivering problem-solving therapy, posted results on ClinicalTrials.gov on 09-23: at 18 weeks, participants coached by the AI improved more than a delayed-treatment control, and those coached by a human improved somewhat more than the AI-coached group on most measures, in unadjusted registry means. On the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale's distress total, the mean change was −5.85 for the AI-coached arm (97 completers), −7.33 for human coaching (48) and −2.76 for the delayed-treatment control (49); the session-level PHQ-9 and GAD-7 changes were −4.56, −5.81 and −1.63, and −4.53, −5.60 and −0.80, in the same order. Three cautions from the record itself: the registry posts descriptive means only, with no between-group tests or confidence intervals; the trial's pre-specified primary outcome was change in a functional-MRI activation measure, on which the arms are not visibly different, with the symptom scales all listed as secondary; and the PHQ-9 and GAD-7 figures come from smaller session-level samples (72, 43 and 30). The 200-person Phase 2 ran 2023 to April 2025 and is NIMH-funded with Penn State, Washington University and Stanford as collaborators; whether a journal paper exists was not checked. Academic, with a human comparator and a delayed-treatment control, it is the kind of evidence this thread asks whether the field can produce. (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05603923)

items.title: OpenAI released MentalHealthBench, an open benchmark for how AI systems handle realistic mental-health conversations, built with more than 80 licensed mental-health experts from more than 20 countries
items.html: OpenAI released MentalHealthBench, an open benchmark for how AI systems handle realistic mental-health conversations, built with more than 80 licensed mental-health experts from more than 20 countries — it scores responses against expert-written rubrics across non-acute, high-acuity and emergency scenarios and adult, teen, caregiver and clinician personas, on safety, seeking context, preserving user agency and actionable guidance. In OpenAI's own paper, OpenAI's newest model, GPT-6 Astra, scored highest at 57.3 (scored as a share of possible rubric points), ahead of Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 at 52.4 and Google's Gemini 3.1 Pro at 32.1; the older GPT-4o scored 32.1. Every author is at OpenAI and the grading is done by OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol, so this is a self-authored, self-graded result rather than an independent ranking; the paper names seeking appropriate context and calibrating urgency as the models' main weaknesses. (OpenAI, OpenAI paper (PDF))

items.title: A Vals AI study of 648 simulated 10-message teen conversations with nine AI models found that 27.5% included a failure on at least one of its most serious safety checks, and that in about 62% of those the failure came later in the exchange rather than in the first reply.
items.html: A Vals AI study of 648 simulated 10-message teen conversations with nine AI models found that 27.5% included a failure on at least one of its most serious safety checks, and that in about 62% of those the failure came later in the exchange rather than in the first reply. The scenarios were written by five clinicians and the teen's messages were simulated by a model; failures included agreeing to help a teen conceal a suicide attempt (4 of 52 conversations where the check applied), giving a diagnosis (109 of 169) and dropping a referral to a doctor or trusted adult. An instruction telling the chatbot the user is 13 to 17 cut the critical-failure share from 31.1% to 11.5% across 270 conversations each way. Models were tested through their APIs, not consumer apps, per-model rates ranged from 9.7% to 47.2% with overlapping ranges that Vals says show no clear ranking, and grading used AI judges with a clinician-reviewed sample. Vals is a third-party evaluator rather than a model maker, and the study was reported the same day as OpenAI's own benchmark. (Vals AI, The Washington Post)

items.title: The CDC's National Center for Health Statistics reported that the final US suicide rate for 2024 was 13.7 per 100,000, down from 14.1 in 2023, with no significant change since 2017.
items.html: The CDC's National Center for Health Statistics reported that the final US suicide rate for 2024 was 13.7 per 100,000, down from 14.1 in 2023, with no significant change since 2017. The decline was concentrated in women 25 and older and in males 15 to 24 (21.2 to 20.2) and 25 to 44 (29.8 to 28.5); firearms remained the leading means for both sexes with no significant change, state rates ran from 5.7 in the District of Columbia to 29.7 in Alaska, and the rate for females 10 to 14 was 2.3 against 2.1 in 2023. (CDC NCHS Data Brief 572)

items.title: The FDA granted Breakthrough Device Designation to NET Recovery's transcutaneous alternating-current stimulation device as an aid in reducing stimulant use in adults with cocaine or methamphetamine use disorder, a condition with no FDA-approved drug or cleared device (company announcement, 09-23).
items.html: The FDA granted Breakthrough Device Designation to NET Recovery's transcutaneous alternating-current stimulation device as an aid in reducing stimulant use in adults with cocaine or methamphetamine use disorder, a condition with no FDA-approved drug or cleared device (company announcement, 09-23). The device is already cleared for opioid-withdrawal symptoms; the designation covers a proposed new indication, buys expedited review and priority status, and does not change clearance requirements. The company says it is still designing a pivotal randomized trial and expects the De Novo pathway, and the stimulant use remains investigational, so this is a regulatory status, not efficacy evidence. (PR Newswire, Psychiatric Times)

items.title: Transcend Therapeutics registered EMPOWER-2 on 09-23 ([NCT07836647](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07836647)), a second 300-patient Phase 3 of TSND-201, its methylone-derived drug for PTSD, with primary completion estimated February 2028.
items.html: Transcend Therapeutics registered EMPOWER-2 on 09-23 (NCT07836647), a second 300-patient Phase 3 of TSND-201, its methylone-derived drug for PTSD, with primary completion estimated February 2028. The design mirrors EMPOWER-1 (NCT07456696, first posted 03-06, primary completion estimated December 2027): weekly dosing for four weeks at one of two dose levels or placebo, an eight-week follow-up, and change in the clinician-rated CAPS-5 as the primary outcome. EMPOWER-2 lists two US sites so far, against 37 for EMPOWER-1. Transcend holds an FDA National Priority Voucher and a Breakthrough Therapy designation for TSND-201. Sponsor-registered design only, no data.

items.title: A Jerusalem Mental Health Center randomized trial compares a closed psychiatric ward built around Soteria principles with a conventional closed ward for adults in acute psychosis ([NCT07836348](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07836348), posted 09-23, enrolling since September 2025).
items.html: A Jerusalem Mental Health Center randomized trial compares a closed psychiatric ward built around Soteria principles with a conventional closed ward for adults in acute psychosis (NCT07836348, posted 09-23, enrolling since September 2025). 200 participants planned; outcomes include psychotic symptom severity, therapeutic alliance, one-year readmission and antipsychotic dose. A rare randomized test of an alternative inpatient model rather than a drug or app.

items.title: US business activity grew at its fastest pace in more than five years in September, S&P Global's flash PMI showed Wednesday: the composite output index rose to 58.4 from 56.0, services reached 58.7 and manufacturing 57.0, while input costs rose at the steepest rate in four years.
items.html: US business activity grew at its fastest pace in more than five years in September, S&P Global's flash PMI showed Wednesday: the composite output index rose to 58.4 from 56.0, services reached 58.7 and manufacturing 57.0, while input costs rose at the steepest rate in four years. Employment grew at a pace not seen for over four years and backlogs of work rose at the sharpest rate since May 2022; S&P Global's Chris Williamson said the data point to annualized growth of around 5%, described "some of the most severe supply chain bottlenecks" of the survey's history outside the pandemic, and called the build-up in pricing power "a worry for the inflation outlook." Treasury yields jumped on the release: as of about 10am ET the 10-year was up more than 7bp at roughly 5.04% and the 2-year up more than 8bp at 4.858%, against 4.96% and 4.71% at Tuesday's close, while the S&P 500 was down 0.3% and the Nasdaq down 0.5%. (S&P Global Flash US PMI, CNBC live updates)

interpretation.mechanism: A composite PMI at a five-year high with input costs at a four-year high and rising backlogs is the demand-led inflation story that Fed presidents Musalem, Goolsbee and Collins made in words this week. It raises the odds the Fed keeps hiking after 09-16, and higher expected policy rates lift the 10-year, which is why yields jumped 7bp on the release. The long end has mostly followed oil and the Fed rather than Treasury's own buyback in September, and this is the Fed leg.

scenarios.direction: The 10-year holds above 5% through Thursday's claims data and the 09-24 SoftBank pricing, with October hike odds rising from about 53%, tightening financing conditions for the AI-debt stack.
scenarios.why: Strong activity plus surging input costs is the data mix that has driven the long end higher before, and oil, which had been offsetting it, bounced back Wednesday morning.
scenarios.precedent: 09-16 to 09-18: after the Fed's hike the 10-year cleared 5% and closed at 5.01% on 09-18, its highest since 2007, tracking the Fed/oil axis (Treasury's Long-End Defense entries).

scenarios.direction: The PMI jump fades as a one-month survey reading, oil resumes its decline on US-Iran diplomacy and the 10-year settles back below 5%.
scenarios.why: Flash PMIs are revised and survey readings are noisy; the 10-year ended Tuesday at 4.96% despite two hawkish Fed speeches because oil fell for a fifth session.
scenarios.precedent: 09-17: an oil-driven rebound pulled the 10-year from above 5% to 4.93% at the close within a day of the post-hike selloff.

items.title: Brent crude reversed its overnight losses Wednesday morning, trading near $100 to $101 a barrel after dipping toward $98.50 — a level that would have extended its losing streak to a sixth session — as Iran's military called President Trump's threat to "annihilate" it a sign of "strategic desperation."
items.html: Brent crude reversed its overnight losses Wednesday morning, trading near $100 to $101 a barrel after dipping toward $98.50 — a level that would have extended its losing streak to a sixth session — as Iran's military called President Trump's threat to "annihilate" it a sign of "strategic desperation." Iran's General Staff warned of strikes "more crushing" than earlier in the nearly seven-month war and Tehran laid out conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, while Trump said US and Iranian delegations met for three hours Tuesday. WTI was near $91 (November contract), up about 1%. Those were morning quotes: Brent went on to settle at $103.08 and WTI at $92.16 (see the market-close bullet below). (CNBC, Iran and Hormuz, CNBC, Treasury yields and oil, CNBC live updates)

items.title: A White House official told Reuters on Wednesday that a Politico report of a planned 90-day ban on US diesel exports was "fake news," after US ultra-low-sulfur diesel futures fell about 5% on the story.
items.html: A White House official told Reuters on Wednesday that a Politico report of a planned 90-day ban on US diesel exports was "fake news," after US ultra-low-sulfur diesel futures fell about 5% on the story. Politico had reported that the administration was working on the ban despite internal disagreement and oil-industry opposition, which would be the first restriction on US energy exports since 2015; Energy Secretary Chris Wright said earlier in the day that an export ban would not work, and European diesel futures rose as much as 7% intraday. Refiners fell on the report (Valero about 2% and Marathon Petroleum about 1%), and analysts warned a ban would do little to ease prices and could worsen supply abroad. In the same Reuters settle report, Brent rose $3.83, or 3.86%, to $103.08 and WTI $1.64, or 1.81%, to $92.16, reversing five sessions of losses after Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian told the UN General Assembly that Tehran would never surrender to the US, and US crude inventories rose 3 million barrels to 426.4 million against an expected 641,000-barrel draw. (Investing.com via Yahoo Finance, Reuters via Yahoo Finance)

items.title: Boston Fed President Susan Collins said she now sees "an increased likelihood" that US inflation stays "notably" above the Fed's 2% target, explaining why she backed last week's quarter-point rate hike, and CME's FedWatch tool put the odds of another 25bp hike at the October meeting at 53.1%.
items.html: Boston Fed President Susan Collins said she now sees "an increased likelihood" that US inflation stays "notably" above the Fed's 2% target, explaining why she backed last week's quarter-point rate hike, and CME's FedWatch tool put the odds of another 25bp hike at the October meeting at 53.1%. Collins' statement is dated Tuesday 09-22 in Reuters' account and was reported by CNBC on Wednesday; she wrote that "somewhat more restrictive" policy will help bring inflation back and that the labor market is "on a better footing"; she joins Musalem and Goolsbee in a hawkish run this week. The ECB's Philip Lane separately told Le Temps that a "second wave of rising energy prices" is likely to keep inflation "higher for longer" in the euro area. (CNBC)

items.title: National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett criticised Federal Reserve policymakers not appointed by President Trump for seeking rate hikes, asking "Why are they hiking" when, he said, recent annualised core inflation is 2%, and said Chairman Kevin Warsh is "managing an unusually partisan Fed."
items.html: National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett criticised Federal Reserve policymakers not appointed by President Trump for seeking rate hikes, asking "Why are they hiking" when, he said, recent annualised core inflation is 2%, and said Chairman Kevin Warsh is "managing an unusually partisan Fed." He spoke Wednesday at Georgetown University, a week after the Fed's first hike since 2023 and a day when Governor Barr said further hikes are likely needed; CNBC describes inflation as still above 3%, so the 2% figure is Hassett's own measure. (Bloomberg, Guavy)

items.title: The 10-year Treasury yield jumped more than 14 basis points Wednesday afternoon to 5.116% — its highest since July 2007 and its biggest one-day move in nearly 18 months — after a Treasury auction of 5-year notes drew weak demand and Fed Governor Michael Barr said "further policy adjustments are likely to be needed" to bring inflation to target.
items.html: The 10-year Treasury yield jumped more than 14 basis points Wednesday afternoon to 5.116% — its highest since July 2007 and its biggest one-day move in nearly 18 months — after a Treasury auction of 5-year notes drew weak demand and Fed Governor Michael Barr said "further policy adjustments are likely to be needed" to bring inflation to target. The auction priced at a 5.033% yield against a six-auction average of 4.186%, with indirect bidders (a group that includes foreign central banks) taking just 54% against a 65% average — "a poor auction with Treasury trying to sell paper into a weak market," per One Point BFG Wealth Partners' Peter Boockvar. The 2-year yield jumped more than 12bp to 4.906%, its highest since May 2024, and the 30-year gained more than 10bp to 5.41%. CME FedWatch's odds of an October 25bp hike rose to about 73% from 55% a day earlier and under 10% a month ago. The S&P 500 was down about 0.7% and the Nasdaq about 1% intraday as of 3pm ET, both off Tuesday's record closes; the average 30-year mortgage rate rose 9bp to 7.26% (Mortgage News Daily), the highest in close to two years. By the close the 10-year had reached 5.135% at its intraday high and ended at 5.11% on Treasury's daily par yield curve (2-year 4.85%, 5-year 4.99%, 30-year 5.40%); Treasury's own auction results confirm the 5-year's 5.033% high yield, a 2.21 bid-to-cover ratio and indirect bidders taking 54% of the $70bn offered. (CNBC, Federal Reserve Board, Barr's 09-23 speech, Yahoo Finance, Treasury auction results via FiscalData)

interpretation.mechanism: A weak 5-year note auction is a direct test of this thread's own question — whether Treasury can keep selling duration at yields the market finds attractive while the Fed is still hiking — and today it failed that test: the auction priced 5.033% against a 4.186% six-auction average, with indirect (largely foreign-official) bidders taking only 54% against a 65% average, i.e. the usual buyer base showed up in smaller size and had to be paid up to clear the issue. Fed Governor Barr's same-day "further policy adjustments are likely to be needed" landed on top of that weak demand and pushed CME FedWatch's October-hike odds from 55% to 70% in a single session, which is the reaction-function logic (hawkish talk plus strong data or weak demand moves the long end) this thread has tracked all month.

scenarios.direction: The 10-year holds above 5.1% into Thursday's jobless claims and SoftBank's bond pricing, and a weak claims read or another hawkish Fed voice pushes it toward 5.2%, raising the funding cost of SoftBank's own OpenAI bond before it prices and tightening financing conditions for the wider AI-debt stack this thread and Son All-In both track.
scenarios.why: Every external-driver move this thread has logged this month has held through at least the next session rather than round-tripping intraday, and SoftBank's own tranche guidance (up to 9.875% on its longest notes) already prices in a higher-for-longer path.
scenarios.precedent: 09-16 to 09-18: the 10-year cleared 5% after the Fed hike and closed at a fresh 2007-era high on 09-18, extending rather than reversing over three sessions (Treasury's Long-End Defense 09-18 entry).

scenarios.direction: The move partly reverses by Thursday's close if claims data comes in soft or oil resumes its decline, the way this month's spikes have repeatedly given back part of a hawkish-data move within a session or two rather than holding the full jump.
scenarios.why: A single weak 5-year auction is not unprecedented and this thread has already logged several same-week reversals (09-17's oil-driven pullback from above 5% to 4.93% is the clearest instance).
scenarios.precedent: 09-17: the 10-year eased from an intraday high above 5% to a 4.93% close the same day CNBC tied an equity rebound to falling oil, on Treasury's Long-End Defense's own 09-17 entry.

interpretation.context_note: capital-context.yaml's rate_regime (asof 08-25) predates the 09-16 hike and the Fed's current 3.75%-4.00% target range; used here for the long-end reaction-function logic only. The auction figures (5.033% yield, 54% indirect) are BMO's read as cited by CNBC, not a direct Treasury auction-results fetch.

items.title: BlackRock's iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF fell 1.6% to $80.46 on Wednesday, a record closing low, more than half below its 2020 peak.
items.html: BlackRock's iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF fell 1.6% to $80.46 on Wednesday, a record closing low, more than half below its 2020 peak. Bloomberg tied the drop to fresh data showing robust US economic activity, which sparked a downturn in government bonds as the yearslong selloff "shows few signs of relenting"; the fund, the largest exchange-traded product tracking long-dated Treasuries, has lost more than half its value since Treasuries rallied on the Fed's pandemic-era rate cuts in 2020. (Bloomberg)

items.title: Investors have begun asking whether 6% is the Treasury yield that hurts stocks, Reuters reported Wednesday, with JPMorgan analysts arguing the equity "breaking threshold" may now sit in the 5.5% to 6.0% range.
items.html: Investors have begun asking whether 6% is the Treasury yield that hurts stocks, Reuters reported Wednesday, with JPMorgan analysts arguing the equity "breaking threshold" may now sit in the 5.5% to 6.0% range. JPMorgan says AI, healthcare and services companies keep spending regardless of borrowing costs, so "the traditional interest-rate channel looks materially less binding." Against that, MSCI's world index halved the last time the 10-year broke 5%, just before the global financial crisis; Invesco's Paul Jackson calculates world stocks start to fall once the 10-year's 12-month average, now about 4.34%, rises through 4.72%; and BlueBay's Mike Bell says the comparison between Treasury yields and the stock market's earnings yield is approaching an inflection point. Last week brought the biggest outflow from emerging-market bond funds in months, and Reuters' Wednesday close report put the S&P 500 at just under 19 times expected earnings, its lowest valuation since 2023 (LSEG). (Reuters via Kitco, Reuters via The Business Times)

interpretation.mechanism: Stocks are priced against the yield on the safe alternative. With the 10-year at 5.11% and the S&P 500 near 19 times expected earnings, an earnings yield of roughly 5.3% (a back-of-envelope figure from Reuters' LSEG multiple) leaves almost no cushion over Treasuries, so each further rise in the long end forces investors to re-run valuation models. JPMorgan's counter is that the companies now driving spending and earnings (AI, healthcare, services) do not cut back when borrowing costs rise, which would push the level at which equities crack toward 5.5% to 6.0%.

scenarios.direction: The 10-year holds above 5% and keeps climbing, valuation models get re-run, and equities give back part of the year's gains.
scenarios.why: Every step of the September rate shock has come from data or supply that has not reversed (the PMI, the weak auction, Fed hike talk), and Invesco's 12-month-average test is still some way from triggering.
scenarios.precedent: Reuters cites the last time the 10-year broke 5%, before the global financial crisis, when MSCI's world index halved; on the map, the 09-16 to 09-18 selloff took the Dow down 631 points as the 10-year cleared 5% (Treasury's Long-End Defense).

scenarios.direction: Equities keep tolerating 5% yields because AI-linked spending is not rate-sensitive, and dip buyers return.
scenarios.why: The Nasdaq set consecutive record closes on 09-21 and 09-22 with the 10-year yield around 5%, which is the behaviour JPMorgan's structural argument predicts.
scenarios.precedent: 09-18 to 09-22: the Nasdaq was flat on 09-18 with the 10-year at 5.01%, then closed at a record 27,244.28 on 09-22 with the 10-year at 4.96% (AI Bear Turn).

interpretation.context_note: capital-context.yaml's rate_regime (asof 08-25) predates the 09-16 hike; it is used for the long-end logic only. The earnings-yield figure is this map's arithmetic on the Reuters multiple, not a sourced number, and the Reuters piece is analysis, not a print.

items.title: Wall Street closed lower Wednesday as the 10-year Treasury yield hit its highest since 2007: the S&P 500 fell 0.75% to 7,706.03, the Nasdaq Composite 1.13% to 26,936.04 and the Dow 352.10 points (0.68%) to 51,511.59, while Brent crude settled up 3.9% at $103.08 a barrel.
items.html: Wall Street closed lower Wednesday as the 10-year Treasury yield hit its highest since 2007: the S&P 500 fell 0.75% to 7,706.03, the Nasdaq Composite 1.13% to 26,936.04 and the Dow 352.10 points (0.68%) to 51,511.59, while Brent crude settled up 3.9% at $103.08 a barrel. Nine of the 11 S&P 500 sectors fell, led by utilities (down 1.7%) and communication services (down 1.5%) per Reuters, with consumer discretionary also down more than 1% per CNBC, while energy (up 1.1%) was the only sector with a real gain; the Russell 2000 dropped about 1.8% to 2,838.66 per AP, and the VIX rose about 7% to roughly 15.2 (15.26 in HDFC Sky's read), still a calm reading. WTI (November) settled up 1.8% at $92.16, US gold futures settled 1.3% lower at $4,318.40 and the dollar index rose about 0.5% to roughly 101.1, its highest since 07-29, with the euro at $1.1405, its weakest since late July. Alphabet fell 3.8% and Amazon 2.2%, and Expedia and Airbnb each lost more than 7%; the Nasdaq had closed at a record on Tuesday, when the S&P 500 finished flat. (HDFC Sky closing report, Reuters via The Business Times, CNBC live updates, Treasury daily par yield curve)

interpretation.mechanism: A rising 10-year yield raises the discount rate on long-duration equities and the cost of the debt behind the AI buildout at the same moment, which is why the Nasdaq (-1.13%) and small caps (the Russell 2000, about -1.8%) fell hardest, utilities (-1.7%) sold off as bond proxies, and only energy, tied to oil, gained.

scenarios.direction: Yields hold above 5.1% through Thursday's 7-year auction and the Fed speakers, and the pullback from the Nasdaq's record extends, with AI-linked names leading the losses.
scenarios.why: Wednesday's move rested on three fresh inputs (the PMI, the weak 5-year auction, Barr's hike call) and none of them reverses by itself; Thursday's early trading extended the slide.
scenarios.precedent: 09-16 to 09-18: after the Fed's hike the Dow fell 631 points, the 10-year cleared 5% and the selloff ran three sessions (Treasury's Long-End Defense 09-18 entry).

scenarios.direction: Oil eases on US-Iran diplomacy, yields drift back below 5.1% and equities recover part of the loss.
scenarios.why: The long end has followed oil all month, and falling oil has been the input that turned hawkish-data selloffs around.
scenarios.precedent: 09-17: a rebound on lower oil pulled the 10-year from above 5% to 4.93% and lifted stocks the same day.

interpretation.context_note: capital-context.yaml's rate_regime (asof 08-25) predates the 09-16 hike; it is used for the long-end logic only. Levels are Wednesday closes and settles.

items.title: Meta's Muse AI agent kept driving a selloff in consumer stocks on Wednesday, with Expedia and Airbnb each down more than 7% while Meta rose 1% to lift its gain for the week to about 12%.
items.html: Meta's Muse AI agent kept driving a selloff in consumer stocks on Wednesday, with Expedia and Airbnb each down more than 7% while Meta rose 1% to lift its gain for the week to about 12%. Reuters' close wrap also had Alphabet down 3.8% and Amazon, which has blocked Muse from its shopping platform, down 2.2%, with the Philadelphia chip index down 1.2%. Its separate tally of the week has TripAdvisor and Booking Holdings down more than 6%, Planet Fitness down 17% and the New York Times down 10%; banks still under pressure (JPMorgan and Wells Fargo down more than 3%, Schwab nearly 5%, insurance brokers Marsh 2.4% and Arthur J. Gallagher 4.6%); and Shopify up 11.4% after saying it would use Muse to process checkouts. Muse has logged 2.8 million downloads in its first two weeks (Sensor Tower), Truist estimates it could add at least $28.5bn of annual revenue for Meta by fiscal 2030, and B. Riley's Art Hogan called the disruption fears for financial firms "far-fetched." (Reuters via The Business Times, Reuters via Global Banking & Finance)

interpretation.mechanism: Muse lets people hand shopping, travel booking and form-filling to an AI agent, so the market is repricing companies whose revenue rests on customer inertia or on being the place a purchase starts: online travel agencies, subscription products, brokers and insurers that an agent can compare on price. Firms the agent transacts through (Shopify, PayPal) and the chip suppliers behind it are bid up, so this is a relative-value repricing of intermediaries against infrastructure rather than a general AI selloff, layered on the same day's rate shock that hit Alphabet and Amazon.

scenarios.direction: The repricing spreads to more intermediary businesses (ride-hailing, delivery, insurance brokers, payments) while Muse downloads keep compounding.
scenarios.why: Reuters cites 2.8 million downloads in two weeks and average daily download growth of 55% over the first ten days; the move has already travelled from financials on Tuesday to travel and subscriptions on Wednesday, and Meta and Shopify are being paid for the same story.
scenarios.precedent: 09-22 to 09-23: the S&P 500 Financials index fell nearly 2% on Tuesday to its lowest close since July, and Expedia and Airbnb each lost more than 7% the next day (AI Bear Turn).

scenarios.direction: The losers stabilise as the disruption fears meet slower real-world adoption, and the rotation fades within days.
scenarios.why: B. Riley's Art Hogan called the fears for financial firms "far-fetched," and Truist's $28.5bn revenue estimate for Meta is a fiscal-2030 figure, so nothing yet shows customers actually switching.
scenarios.precedent: 09-23: a GuruFocus read had the financials ETF down only about 0.25% on Wednesday afternoon after Tuesday's near-2% drop, although Reuters said financials stayed under pressure (AI Bear Turn).

interpretation.context_note: capital-context.yaml has no reading on consumer-AI disruption; this uses the map's ai-trade-bear-turn thread and Reuters' 09-23 close wrap and winners-and-losers piece. Weekly moves are as of Wednesday's close.

items.title: Chip stocks and the biggest AI cloud spenders fell together on Wednesday as Treasury yields hit their highest since 2007: Nvidia closed down 1.4% at $225.51 and Alphabet fell 3.8% to $337.83.
items.html: Chip stocks and the biggest AI cloud spenders fell together on Wednesday as Treasury yields hit their highest since 2007: Nvidia closed down 1.4% at $225.51 and Alphabet fell 3.8% to $337.83. Reuters put the Philadelphia chip index down 1.2% and Nvidia down 1.5%. The larger drop was in a hyperscaler and the move tracked the rate shock, so the day reads as a rates selloff rather than a rotation out of chipmakers into cloud spenders. (Barron's, biggo Finance)

items.title: SoftBank closed order books at noon ET Wednesday on its $11bn-plus junk-bond sale to fund its OpenAI stake, tightening guidance to 8.75%-8.875% on $1bn of 3.5-year notes, 9.375%-9.5% on $4.5bn of 5.5-year notes and 9.75%-9.875% on $4.5bn of 7.5-year notes — record highs for any SoftBank dollar bond — on more than $20bn of orders, with pricing now expected Thursday 09-24 and settlement 09-29 (the terms were set that evening; see Deals & filings).
items.html: SoftBank closed order books at noon ET Wednesday on its $11bn-plus junk-bond sale to fund its OpenAI stake, tightening guidance to 8.75%-8.875% on $1bn of 3.5-year notes, 9.375%-9.5% on $4.5bn of 5.5-year notes and 9.75%-9.875% on $4.5bn of 7.5-year notes — record highs for any SoftBank dollar bond — on more than $20bn of orders, with pricing now expected Thursday 09-24 and settlement 09-29 (the terms were set that evening; see Deals & filings). The low end of the shortest tranche (8.75%) is close to the 8.5% average yield on B-rated US corporate debt, well above the 6.55% BB-category average despite SoftBank's own BB+ rating from S&P and Fitch — a sign issuers are paying up regardless of rating as the AI-debt stack competes for the same buyers. (Seoul Economic Daily, citing Bloomberg, The Standard, citing term sheet)

items.title: Xi Jinping landed at Joint Base Andrews on Wednesday evening, met at the foot of the aircraft steps by President Trump, for a state visit that opens with Thursday's summit, bringing a much smaller Chinese business delegation than expected.
items.html: Xi Jinping landed at Joint Base Andrews on Wednesday evening, met at the foot of the aircraft steps by President Trump, for a state visit that opens with Thursday's summit, bringing a much smaller Chinese business delegation than expected. Reports last week anticipated a large CEO contingent; state media listed only family members and political aides plus Politburo member Cai Qi and Foreign Minister Wang Yi, and the South China Morning Post attributed the pared-back list to a lack of progress on deals. Trade, rare earths, AI and the Iran war are expected on the agenda, and Trump and Xi are due at a Thursday state dinner with US tech executives including Nvidia's Jensen Huang, OpenAI's Sam Altman and Google's Sundar Pichai; no Chinese counterparts are expected among the executives. Xi's schedule runs through Friday. (CNBC, Yahoo Finance)

items.title: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Wednesday that the US-China trade truce will be extended by two months, to January 10, as Xi landed in Washington, well short of the six months or longer many had expected.
items.html: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Wednesday that the US-China trade truce will be extended by two months, to January 10, as Xi landed in Washington, well short of the six months or longer many had expected. Bessent told Fox News that Beijing still needs to deliver more, and the truce agreed in October 2025, which kept tariffs lower and rare-earth exports flowing, had been due to expire in November. Chinese state media did not immediately confirm the extension; CSIS's Scott Kennedy read the short extension as a sign Washington is unsatisfied with China's offers, and the European Chamber of Commerce in China noted an extension does not fix the lack of a standard rare-earth licensing process. Trump and Xi could also meet at the APEC meeting in Shenzhen in November and the G20 in Miami in December. (CNBC)

items.title: Prime Minister Mark Carney told the New York Times he has studied the possibility of US-led military action against Canada, calling it "extreme tail risk" and "not a base case."
items.html: Prime Minister Mark Carney told the New York Times he has studied the possibility of US-led military action against Canada, calling it "extreme tail risk" and "not a base case." In the interview, published Wednesday 09-23, he said "it would be irresponsible not to" prepare, that he and Trump still speak "frequently" even after trade talks collapsed in mid-August, and that Canada is looking at reducing its reliance on Starlink and at alternatives to a full F-35 fleet. The day after talks broke down Trump imposed 50% duties on about $28 billion of Canadian goods, and Canada retaliated in early September. (Global News, New York Times)

items.title: The US Treasury scheduled a buyback of up to $6 billion of 20- to 30-year bonds for Thursday 09-24, its first operation at the tripled $6bn ceiling in the longest maturities; the previous $6bn operation, in 10- to 20-year debt on 09-10, bought only $5.19 billion.
items.html: The US Treasury scheduled a buyback of up to $6 billion of 20- to 30-year bonds for Thursday 09-24, its first operation at the tripled $6bn ceiling in the longest maturities; the previous $6bn operation, in 10- to 20-year debt on 09-10, bought only $5.19 billion. It lands a day after the 10-year jumped to 5.116%; Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has said he acts only when market prices deviate from equilibrium. (BigGo Finance, US Treasury buyback operations data)

items.title: Pima County, Arizona's Board of Supervisors approved a 120-day moratorium on new data-center development in a 3-2 vote on 09-22, citing energy, air pollution, water stress, noise and waste heat.
items.html: Pima County, Arizona's Board of Supervisors approved a 120-day moratorium on new data-center development in a 3-2 vote on 09-22, citing energy, air pollution, water stress, noise and waste heat. It exempts the county's already-approved project and adds another US jurisdiction to the pauses that bear on data-center financing. (Arizona Luminaria)

items.title: Maryland Gov. Wes Moore signed an executive order creating one state review process for every data center of 25 megawatts or more that seeks a state permit, incentive or letter of support, without imposing a moratorium.
items.html: Maryland Gov. Wes Moore signed an executive order creating one state review process for every data center of 25 megawatts or more that seeks a state permit, incentive or letter of support, without imposing a moratorium. A new Data Center Task Force in the Governor's Office will give each project a public determination of "Aligned," "Conditionally Aligned" or "Not Aligned" and keep a monthly public dashboard of projected power and water use, and Moore said he will ask the General Assembly to repeal the 2020 data-center sales-tax exemption, days after saying he would sign a moratorium if lawmakers passed one. The order became an election issue within hours: his Republican opponent Dan Cox called the timing a political stunt, and Moore's campaign noted the exemption was a 2020 bill Cox sponsored. (Maryland Governor's Office, WTOP)

items.title: A Scripps News Group investigation documents local officials threatened, resigning and, in some cases, residents arrested in data-center disputes across the country, including officials in Michigan townships that had no project in development.
items.html: A Scripps News Group investigation documents local officials threatened, resigning and, in some cases, residents arrested in data-center disputes across the country, including officials in Michigan townships that had no project in development. Examples include Saline Township's treasurer resigning in tears over threats, Tyrone Township officials receiving death-threat voicemails after an edited meeting clip spread, an Indianapolis councilman finding bullet holes in his door and a "No data centers" note in April, two Illinois men charged over Facebook threats, and police removing residents from public meetings in Claremore, Oklahoma and Emporia, Kansas. (Scripps News)

items.title: Japan's 10-year government bond yield rose as high as 3.075% in Tokyo on Thursday, the highest in 30 years, tracking the US Treasury selloff, while the yen slid to the low 158s per dollar before recovering on talk of intervention.
items.html: Japan's 10-year government bond yield rose as high as 3.075% in Tokyo on Thursday, the highest in 30 years, tracking the US Treasury selloff, while the yen slid to the low 158s per dollar before recovering on talk of intervention. The benchmark 10-year JGB gained about 8bp (3.062% in CNBC's read) to its highest since August 1996 and the 30-year rose nearly 8bp to 4.147%; UK gilt and German Bund yields also rose, with various European yields at fresh multi-year highs. NHK reported the yen strengthened to the upper 157 range later in the session on speculation authorities may step in, a week after rate checks with currency dealers, a step that often precedes intervention; the Bank of Japan raised rates a quarter point to 1.25%, on a 7-2 vote, last week. (NHK, CNBC)

interpretation.mechanism: Higher US yields spill into Japanese bonds, and with the yen near 158 the wide US-Japan rate gap keeps it weak, so authorities' rate checks are the only brake: a JGB yield at a 30-year high raises pressure on the carry trade and on Japanese AI-linked equities that borrow against rates.

scenarios.direction: USD/JPY presses toward 159-160, Japanese authorities intervene or escalate their warnings, and a sharp yen rally unwinds carry trades.
scenarios.why: Rate checks last week and the finance minister's warning show the threshold is being watched, and the hawkish Fed repricing widens the gap that pushes the pair toward it.
scenarios.precedent: 09-08: a yen carry unwind took USD/JPY from 156.20 to 153.93 and the Nikkei down 1,130 points in a session (The Cross-Border Rate Leg).

scenarios.direction: JGB yields keep climbing with Treasuries and hit Japanese AI-linked stocks, as SoftBank, Kioxia and Arm fell together on the last such day.
scenarios.why: The 10-year JGB is at its highest since 1996 and the transmission runs from rates into the long-duration equities that carry the AI trade.
scenarios.precedent: 08-19: the 10-year JGB pushed toward its highest yield since 1996 and took Nikkei, SoftBank, Kioxia and Arm down together (capital-context rate_regime).

interpretation.context_note: Yen and JGB levels are Thursday-morning Tokyo reads from NHK and CNBC, not closes; capital-context's rate_regime notes its own BOJ leg is thin.

items.title: The average yield on Bloomberg's Global Aggregate Treasuries index rose 8 basis points to 3.99% on Wednesday, a level not seen since 2007, on the index's biggest one-day loss since May.
items.html: The average yield on Bloomberg's Global Aggregate Treasuries index rose 8 basis points to 3.99% on Wednesday, a level not seen since 2007, on the index's biggest one-day loss since May. The index is down about 2.4% in 2026 after a 6.8% gain in 2025. Swaps fully price three quarter-point Fed hikes over the next year with significant hedging for a fourth, and the ICE BofA MOVE index of US bond volatility climbed to its highest since March. On Thursday Australia's three-year yield jumped 13 basis points to 5.07%, its highest since May 2011, and New Zealand's two-year yield rose as much as 17 basis points to just under 4%; strategists at JPMorgan and KKR see scope for US yields to climb further. (Bloomberg via The Business Times)

items.title: Japanese Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said Thursday in Tokyo that the principles behind the coordinated Japan-US currency intervention of July 31 remain in place, signalling readiness to act again if yen moves become disorderly.
items.html: Japanese Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said Thursday in Tokyo that the principles behind the coordinated Japan-US currency intervention of July 31 remain in place, signalling readiness to act again if yen moves become disorderly. The yen sat near 158 per dollar after last week's Bank of Japan hike failed to reassure investors; Japan's Ministry of Finance said on August 3 that it bought yen in coordination with the US Treasury, "will not hesitate to conduct further joint intervention," and plans to use the Fed's FIMA repo facility, and Katayama declined to comment on levels. (Reuters, Traders Union, Japan Ministry of Finance)

items.title: The Swiss National Bank held its policy rate at 0% on Thursday, defying the tightening cycle the Fed, the European Central Bank and the Bank of Japan have begun, with traders pricing roughly even odds of a December hike.
items.html: The Swiss National Bank held its policy rate at 0% on Thursday, defying the tightening cycle the Fed, the European Central Bank and the Bank of Japan have begun, with traders pricing roughly even odds of a December hike. Swiss inflation was 0.8% in August, inside the bank's 0%-2% range, and traders put the chance the SNB starts raising rates by early 2027 above 90%; CNBC notes the Bank of Canada and the Bank of England are expected to follow the hiking trio later this year. (CNBC)

items.title: Global debt rose by $10 trillion in the first half of 2026 to top $365 trillion, the Institute of International Finance said Wednesday, warning of a "vicious cycle" as the US, Japan, France and the UK carry deficits and interest bills more typical of debt-distressed emerging markets.
items.html: Global debt rose by $10 trillion in the first half of 2026 to top $365 trillion, the Institute of International Finance said Wednesday, warning of a "vicious cycle" as the US, Japan, France and the UK carry deficits and interest bills more typical of debt-distressed emerging markets. Advanced economies paid over $3.3 trillion in interest on internationally traded government bonds last year, more than global spending on AI ($2.6 trillion), defense ($3.1 trillion) or clean energy ($2.3 trillion); the OECD said in a report the same day that rising yields show the need to contain and reallocate government spending. (CNBC)

items.title: SoftBank priced $11.1bn of dollar and euro bonds to fund the last $10bn of its $30bn OpenAI follow-on investment: $1bn of 3.5-year notes at 8.625%, $4.5bn of 5.5-year notes at 9.25% and $4.5bn of 7.5-year notes at 9.75%, plus two €500m tranches at 7.125% and 8%.
items.html: SoftBank priced $11.1bn of dollar and euro bonds to fund the last $10bn of its $30bn OpenAI follow-on investment: $1bn of 3.5-year notes at 8.625%, $4.5bn of 5.5-year notes at 9.25% and $4.5bn of 7.5-year notes at 9.75%, plus two €500m tranches at 7.125% and 8%. The 3.5- and 5.5-year tranches priced inside Wednesday's guidance (8.75%-8.875% and 9.375%-9.5%) and the 7.5-year tranche at the low end of its 9.75%-9.875% range, after more than $20bn of orders; Reuters described it as the largest high-yield corporate bond sale on record. SoftBank's release, dated Thursday in Tokyo, says the notes are rated BB+ by S&P and Fitch, settle 09-29, and that it expects to cancel the remaining $10bn of its bridge facility; the $10bn OpenAI payment is expected to close 10-01. SoftBank's Tokyo shares rose as much as 7% at Thursday's open, after a three-day holiday, then gave back nearly all of the gain by mid-morning. (SoftBank Group release, Invezz, CNBC live updates, Reuters)

interpretation.mechanism: A BB+ issuer paid 9.75% for seven-year money to fund an unlisted-lab stake, with the base rate (10-year at 5.11%) doing much of the lifting: pricing at the low end of guidance on $20bn-plus of orders shows buyers exist at that yield, and the coupon shows what the OpenAI exposure costs to carry.

scenarios.direction: The tight pricing reopens the window for other AI borrowers, and lease-backed junk deals such as the CoreWeave-tied $1.1bn bond clear at similar yields this week.
scenarios.why: An oversubscribed $11bn high-yield deal signals depth in the buyer base that other AI-linked issuers can borrow against.
scenarios.precedent: 09-21: Meta's first junk bond, $2.3bn at 8.25%, drew about $10bn of demand (Circular Financing, 09-22 digest).

scenarios.direction: The notes slip below par in secondary trading as Treasury yields rise and AI credit stays wider than the rest of the market.
scenarios.why: Reuters reported AI-issuer spreads near 115bp against 78bp for broad investment-grade, and a rising base rate compounds that.
scenarios.precedent: 09-22: the Jane Street-leased Oklahoma bond issued near 8.9% traded at 11.3%, and Meta's Hyperion bond fell to 94.4 cents (AI Debt Gets Rated).

interpretation.context_note: Coupons and dates are from SoftBank's own release; the $20bn order figure is Bloomberg's preliminary read as relayed by secondary coverage.

items.title: A Goldman Sachs-led group raised about $1.1bn in a junk-bond sale on Wednesday to fund a 76-megawatt data center near Richmond, Virginia, whose entire capacity is contracted to CoreWeave under a 15-year lease worth $2.94bn.
items.html: A Goldman Sachs-led group raised about $1.1bn in a junk-bond sale on Wednesday to fund a 76-megawatt data center near Richmond, Virginia, whose entire capacity is contracted to CoreWeave under a 15-year lease worth $2.94bn. The five-year notes, sold by a developer sponsored by affiliates of Blue Owl Capital, priced at 98.5 cents on the dollar to yield 9.25%, roughly 2.7 percentage points above the average yield on similarly rated debt tracked by Bloomberg, according to a person familiar with the deal; it is the latest lease-backed financing tied to the AI cloud provider, coming a day after CoreWeave closed its own upsized $4.2bn convertible. (Bloomberg, Briefs Finance)

items.title: Inference-cloud startups Baseten and Modal Labs are both in talks to raise at sharply higher valuations, Baseten at $26bn and Modal at $15bn, Bloomberg reported Wednesday.
items.html: Inference-cloud startups Baseten and Modal Labs are both in talks to raise at sharply higher valuations, Baseten at $26bn and Modal at $15bn, Bloomberg reported Wednesday. Axios first reported Baseten's talks on Tuesday 09-22; Bloomberg says the $26bn is up from $13bn in June, when Baseten raised a $1.5bn Series F, and that Modal raised $355m at a $4.65bn valuation four months ago, so $15bn would roughly triple it. Both are talks, not closed rounds, and the coverage read carried no comment from either company. (Bloomberg, Axios Pro, Tech Funding News on Modal, Business Wire on Baseten's Series F)

urls.label: Business Wire on Baseten's Series F

items.title: Mirendil, the self-improving-AI research startup founded by former Anthropic, xAI and OpenAI staff, is in talks to raise up to $1bn at a $5bn valuation, five times its valuation three months ago, Bloomberg reported Tuesday.
items.html: Mirendil, the self-improving-AI research startup founded by former Anthropic, xAI and OpenAI staff, is in talks to raise up to $1bn at a $5bn valuation, five times its valuation three months ago, Bloomberg reported Tuesday. Kleiner Perkins may lead the round and Andreessen Horowitz, which co-led the seed, is also negotiating; the San Francisco company, founded in December 2025, still has no public product. Axios's Pro Rata newsletter carried the report Wednesday. (Bloomberg, Tech Funding News)

items.title: Credit default swaps tied to Nvidia are now among the most traded in the US market as investors hedge its debt: protection on $6.9 billion of debt changed hands in the past six months, against $640 million in the six months before.
items.html: Credit default swaps tied to Nvidia are now among the most traded in the US market as investors hedge its debt: protection on $6.9 billion of debt changed hands in the past six months, against $640 million in the six months before. The figures come from S&P Dow Jones Indices' Nicholas Godec, citing DTCC data, and follow Nvidia's $25 billion bond sale in June. (Bloomberg)

items.title: One unnamed customer accounted for 73% of Nscale's 2025 revenue and 52% of its first-half 2026 revenue, the company's IPO filing says, and the Financial Times reported the customer is a ByteDance-linked Singapore unit mentioned only in an appendix.
items.html: One unnamed customer accounted for 73% of Nscale's 2025 revenue and 52% of its first-half 2026 revenue, the company's IPO filing says, and the Financial Times reported the customer is a ByteDance-linked Singapore unit mentioned only in an appendix. The S-1 says the same customer should fall below 20% of revenue in 2026 as Microsoft (up to about $43.8bn of statements of work through 2033) and Anthropic (about $44.6bn) contracts scale, which together make up roughly $88bn of its $103.4bn contracted backlog; the filing's own text does not name the customer. (The Decoder, citing the Financial Times, Nscale S-1 on SEC EDGAR)
items.source: The Decoder, citing the Financial Times

urls.label: The Decoder, citing the Financial Times

items.title: Nvidia-backed data-center operator Firmus expects to lose US$77 million in the half ending December on a pro forma basis, according to two people who saw a draft prospectus, as it prepares a US$5 billion IPO due to start trading on the Australian exchange on October 22.
items.html: Nvidia-backed data-center operator Firmus expects to lose US$77 million in the half ending December on a pro forma basis, according to two people who saw a draft prospectus, as it prepares a US$5 billion IPO due to start trading on the Australian exchange on October 22. Reuters said the float would be Australia's second largest after Telstra in 1997, local media put the post-IPO value at up to US$60bn, the draft calls Firmus historically loss-making and says its data centres could earn US$5bn a year within five years, and Nvidia, Meta and OpenAI are among its customers; bookbuilding starts October 6 and the prospectus is due October 8. (Reuters via KLSE Screener, Reuters)

items.title: DeepSeek's annualised revenue run rate has reached about $1 billion, more than double a few months ago, The Information reported, and the company is aiming to raise about 50 billion yuan ($7.45 billion) at a 500 billion yuan valuation by the end of October.
items.html: DeepSeek's annualised revenue run rate has reached about $1 billion, more than double a few months ago, The Information reported, and the company is aiming to raise about 50 billion yuan ($7.45 billion) at a 500 billion yuan valuation by the end of October. Reuters says CEO Liang Wenfeng shared the revenue figure with investors and describes the raise as an IPO ahead of a Shanghai Stock Exchange listing, while The Information's headline calls it a fundraising; revenue growth was partly driven by raising model prices 2.3 to 4.5 times, and DeepSeek devotes more than 70% of its computing capacity to training. Reuters reported earlier this month that DeepSeek had hired CITIC Securities to prepare for a possible STAR Market IPO, with timing, valuation and size undecided; it could not verify The Information's figures and DeepSeek did not comment. (Reuters via The Economic Times, The Information)

items.title: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang said AI infrastructure supply and demand will "be inverted again" at some point, but "it's not going to happen next year" or "in the next couple, two, three years," and that the turn would arrive as a "period of digestion" lasting six months to a year.
items.html: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang said AI infrastructure supply and demand will "be inverted again" at some point, but "it's not going to happen next year" or "in the next couple, two, three years," and that the turn would arrive as a "period of digestion" lasting six months to a year. Asked on the Ezra Klein Show whether the boom could follow the dot-com bust, he described it as "the nature of markets"; the remarks are as quoted by Benzinga and come from the executive whose company's chip sales, equity stakes and lease guarantees depend on the buildout continuing. (Benzinga, New York Times)

items.title: Big Tech companies have issued up to $300bn of guarantees backing AI data centres and chips over the past year, keeping most of the exposure off their balance sheets, the Financial Times reported on Sunday 09-20.
items.html: Big Tech companies have issued up to $300bn of guarantees backing AI data centres and chips over the past year, keeping most of the exposure off their balance sheets, the Financial Times reported on Sunday 09-20. The two largest disclosed pieces are in the companies' own quarterly filings: Alphabet's June-quarter 10-Q (filed 07-23) shows credit-derivative backstops on data-center leases with a maximum payout of $43.8bn, up from $16.9bn at year-end and carried at an $815m liability, plus $7.6bn of financial guarantees and an agreed $24.1bn of further backstops; Meta's (filed 07-30) shows a residual value guarantee of about $28bn on its Hyperion venture with Blue Owl, with no liability recorded because payment is "not probable," and a planned $13bn one on El Paso. (Financial Times, Alphabet 10-Q, Meta 10-Q, Startup Fortune summary of the FT)

urls.label: Startup Fortune summary of the FT

items.title: Nvidia agreed to guarantee up to $860.3 million of Nscale's rent for the first five years of a Ward County, Texas data-center lease, Nscale's IPO filing of 09-18 discloses, with Nscale holding $470 million in escrow as recourse for Nvidia and paying Nvidia in warrants for the guarantee.
items.html: Nvidia agreed to guarantee up to $860.3 million of Nscale's rent for the first five years of a Ward County, Texas data-center lease, Nscale's IPO filing of 09-18 discloses, with Nscale holding $470 million in escrow as recourse for Nvidia and paying Nvidia in warrants for the guarantee. The S-1 shows the guarantee dates from October 14 2025, the warrants cover up to 9.48 million Series B shares valued at $60 million, Nvidia also holds $300 million of pre-Series C SAFEs, its $1.0bn share of Nscale's $3.1bn convertible closes around November 16, and Nvidia is itself a customer: a July 2025 agreement has Nscale supplying it $1.2bn of reserved GPU capacity. The guarantee, SAFEs and convertible alone add to about $2.2bn. (Nscale S-1 on SEC EDGAR)

items.title: JPMorgan chief executive Jamie Dimon said spending across the hyperscaler ecosystem has more than doubled from about $300 billion last year to around $700 billion this year and could reach $1 trillion next year.
items.html: JPMorgan chief executive Jamie Dimon said spending across the hyperscaler ecosystem has more than doubled from about $300 billion last year to around $700 billion this year and could reach $1 trillion next year. Speaking to CNBC-TV18 at JPMorgan's India investor conference on 09-21, he called the surge "like 1% increase to GDP each year" and warned it may also add to inflation, a direct counterweight to the view that AI infrastructure capex is peaking, from the head of a lender to the sector. (CNBC, CNBC-TV18)

items.title: OpenAI asked a Texas federal judge on 09-22 for summary judgment against SpaceXAI and X Corp.'s antitrust suit over Apple's ChatGPT integration, quoting SpaceX's IPO registration statement that Grok is "among the fastest-advancing frontier models relative to peers, including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google."
items.html: OpenAI asked a Texas federal judge on 09-22 for summary judgment against SpaceXAI and X Corp.'s antitrust suit over Apple's ChatGPT integration, quoting SpaceX's IPO registration statement that Grok is "among the fastest-advancing frontier models relative to peers, including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google." The 59-page brief in X Corp. v. Apple (N.D. Tex., Judge Mark Pittman) notes that SpaceX, "now valued at $2 trillion," told investors in its May 20 filing (amended June 3) it holds a "formidable competitive advantage" and made no mention of the Apple agreement or the lawsuit; sealed portions were allowed 09-23, and Reuters reports a trial set for January. The docket shows the filing is a motion for summary judgment, not the motion to dismiss some headlines called it. (OpenAI brief, CourtListener, CourtListener docket)

items.title: Tigrayan forces seized airports across the Tigray region and launched an offensive against federal positions in the neighbouring Afar and Amhara regions early Wednesday, Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's adviser Getachew Reda said; Tigray's authorities say they are fighting a "defensive war" against a federal "invasion."
items.html: Tigrayan forces seized airports across the Tigray region and launched an offensive against federal positions in the neighbouring Afar and Amhara regions early Wednesday, Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's adviser Getachew Reda said; Tigray's authorities say they are fighting a "defensive war" against a federal "invasion." Ethiopian Airlines suspended flights to three northern Tigray airports, residents of Mekelle told the BBC that local forces took over its airport from federal police, and clashes were reported in Afar at Abala and Berahle. AFP reported that humanitarian staff in Afar said fighting between the TPLF and federal forces broke out at Abala and Erebti late Tuesday, and a foreign security source said the TPLF controlled Abala. The fighting comes three days after the Tigray People's Liberation Front announced an alliance with six other armed groups to remove Abiy's government, and a day after Tigrayan authorities said federal strikes killed at least 14 in Alamata; the BBC could not independently verify either side's account of who attacked first. The International Crisis Group's Alan Boswell said "if we're not all the way back into something like a full war, we are very, very close," and that Eritrea's alignment with the TPLF threatens to make it regional. (Al Jazeera, AFP, BBC News, Africanews, AFP)

items.title: TPLF Vice President Amanuel Assefa told AFP "it is the beginning of the war," saying Tigrayan forces took prisoner the federal police guarding Mekelle, Shire and Axum airports and that ground forces attacked Tigray from the south and east, while the African Union called for "immediate deescalation."
items.html: TPLF Vice President Amanuel Assefa told AFP "it is the beginning of the war," saying Tigrayan forces took prisoner the federal police guarding Mekelle, Shire and Axum airports and that ground forces attacked Tigray from the south and east, while the African Union called for "immediate deescalation." A former senior TPLF official told AFP the rebels control several towns in the region and federal forces are "fast-retreating" — claims AFP could not independently confirm and Addis Ababa had not yet commented on. Conflict-monitoring group ACLED said Tigrayan forces also attacked positions in Amhara alongside the Fano militia, part of the new anti-government alliance, warning "today's episode will cause worry that the other agents in the alliance are about to act in their areas." (AFP via Courthouse News)

items.title: The East African bloc IGAD has called for hostilities in northern Ethiopia to cease and direct dialogue to resume, and the UN has said it was concerned by the new armed coalition and reports of drone attacks.
items.html: The East African bloc IGAD has called for hostilities in northern Ethiopia to cease and direct dialogue to resume, and the UN has said it was concerned by the new armed coalition and reports of drone attacks. UN Secretary-General António Guterres separately warned in a statement dated 09-23 that the fighting could become "broader and more devastating" and called for maximum restraint, and the African Union activated mediation by former Nigerian president Olusegun Obasanjo, who helped broker the 2022 Pretoria agreement, according to Kulu Media's account of the statements. The alliance said in its own statement that the federal government was attacking its members on several fronts. (Al Jazeera, Kulu Media, citing the UN statement)

urls.label: Kulu Media, citing the UN statement

items.title: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, addressing the UN General Assembly, answered Trump's speech directly: "The US president described us as terrorists. We have been the victims of terrorism," saying the US "bombed a school" and that Iran "responded, but we did not hit civilian populations."
items.html: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, addressing the UN General Assembly, answered Trump's speech directly: "The US president described us as terrorists. We have been the victims of terrorism," saying the US "bombed a school" and that Iran "responded, but we did not hit civilian populations." The US delegation walked out as he spoke. On Hormuz he said "we cannot let some have free access and gain their interest from a waterway, while at the same time using that waterway to impose their aggressions upon us... to forbid us access to our own waterways," and warned that any "expansion of warfare will not result in security"; on the nuclear file, "no nuclear weapons and no limitations to peaceful nuclear technology." The Guardian's live blog had reported the speech only up to those passages when this was written, and no offer of specific terms had appeared in it. (Guardian live blog)

items.title: Iranian flights to Baghdad and Muscat stop from midnight local time Wednesday as US secondary sanctions on aviation services take effect, Iran's Civil Aviation Organization said, with Baghdad-bound flights diverted to Najaf.
items.html: Iranian flights to Baghdad and Muscat stop from midnight local time Wednesday as US secondary sanctions on aviation services take effect, Iran's Civil Aviation Organization said, with Baghdad-bound flights diverted to Najaf. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Monday that anyone who fuels, services or sells tickets to Iranian carriers "will be knocked out of the dollar system"; OFAC's wind-down licence for Iranian-airspace overflight payments and related services expired at 12:01am EDT on 09-23. Iran said remaining international flights, including to Istanbul, operate as scheduled; Iraqi and Omani authorities had not commented. (Al Jazeera, Guardian)

items.title: In his full UN General Assembly speech, Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian held up photos of assassinated former Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and of schoolgirls killed in an alleged US strike on a school in Minab, saying "they hit us, but we did not bow our heads or bend the knee," while also saying "Iran extends its hands towards the world."
items.html: In his full UN General Assembly speech, Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian held up photos of assassinated former Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and of schoolgirls killed in an alleged US strike on a school in Minab, saying "they hit us, but we did not bow our heads or bend the knee," while also saying "Iran extends its hands towards the world." A US delegation official walked out as he spoke and Israel's delegation boycotted it; Iran researcher Negar Mortazavi told Al Jazeera the speech signalled Tehran "may even show some flexibility" toward a deal beyond the expired June memorandum, while former US diplomat Joey Hood called it "a lost opportunity" for a concrete new offer that would have put Trump "on the backfoot." No published boundaries, coordinates or NOTAM/NAVTEX for the "restricted zone" Iran announced for the Strait of Hormuz on 09-07 were found this pass. (Al Jazeera)

items.title: A senior Iranian official told Reuters on Wednesday that Iran and the United States remain "far apart" on ending the war but that diplomacy must continue, saying Tehran is reviewing Washington's response to its proposals on lifting the US naval blockade and reopening the Strait of Hormuz and that "there are still many differences."
items.html: A senior Iranian official told Reuters on Wednesday that Iran and the United States remain "far apart" on ending the war but that diplomacy must continue, saying Tehran is reviewing Washington's response to its proposals on lifting the US naval blockade and reopening the Strait of Hormuz and that "there are still many differences." Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei said the indirect talks held through Qatari mediators on the sidelines of the General Assembly were "not anything new" and that Iran had maintained its demands — an end to the blockade and the release of frozen assets. European Council President Antonio Costa said he had spoken with Pezeshkian and urged Iran to restore freedom of navigation, halt strikes on its neighbours and resume cooperation with the UN nuclear watchdog. (RFE/RL live blog, citing Reuters, Naharnet, citing Baghaei)

items.title: Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei warned on Wednesday that airports in neighbouring countries that cooperate with the US ban on Iranian airlines "will no longer be able to operate flights" to Iran, as Georgia and Azerbaijan confirmed suspending flights from Iran.
items.html: Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei warned on Wednesday that airports in neighbouring countries that cooperate with the US ban on Iranian airlines "will no longer be able to operate flights" to Iran, as Georgia and Azerbaijan confirmed suspending flights from Iran. Rezaei did not say whether Tehran's response would be diplomatic, economic or military; Al Jazeera notes Iran cannot legally decide whether another country's airport takes its aircraft, but that it showed in the war's opening months it could bring Gulf air travel to a near-halt by striking Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman and Jordan. Flights to Baghdad and Muscat had already stopped, and several connections to Turkey and China continued while many others were cancelled. (Al Jazeera, Al Jazeera on the overland shift)

urls.label: Al Jazeera on the overland shift

items.title: US Central Command said its forces had redirected 115 commercial vessels as of 09-23 under what it calls America's "steel wall blockade" of Iranian ports.
items.html: US Central Command said its forces had redirected 115 commercial vessels as of 09-23 under what it calls America's "steel wall blockade" of Iranian ports. CENTCOM posted the figure on X; Gulf News calls it the renewed naval blockade, and Iran International adds that any effort to end the war faces apparent divisions inside Tehran over who has authority to negotiate. (Gulf News, Iran International)

items.title: The Antigua and Barbuda-flagged bulk carrier Cape Dao was struck twice on its port side about 2.5 nautical miles off Oman's Musandam peninsula at around 6:30am UTC Wednesday, killing an Indian seafarer, 26-year-old wiper Suraj Yadav, and setting the engine room on fire; a Royal Navy of Oman vessel evacuated the 27 surviving crew.
items.html: The Antigua and Barbuda-flagged bulk carrier Cape Dao was struck twice on its port side about 2.5 nautical miles off Oman's Musandam peninsula at around 6:30am UTC Wednesday, killing an Indian seafarer, 26-year-old wiper Suraj Yadav, and setting the engine room on fire; a Royal Navy of Oman vessel evacuated the 27 surviving crew. UKMTO reported the vessel struck by an unknown projectile, on fire and adrift, and Oman's Maritime Security Center reported the incident without naming an attacker; India condemned the attack. The ship, sailing from the UAE toward India with 28 crew, was hit once in the accommodation area and once near the engine room, according to gCaptain. MarineRadar reports two further vessels — the crude tanker LR Stephanie and the LPG tanker Al Maryah — were also struck by unknown projectiles the same day, both continuing without a tow; that account rests on security sources and a single outlet. No party had claimed any of the attacks in the coverage read. (gCaptain, India Today, MarineRadar)

items.title: Iranian state media said Brigadier General Hossein Zarifi, commander of a Revolutionary Guards operational base in Saravan, in Sistan-Baluchestan province on the Pakistani border, was killed Wednesday in clashes with armed men, with reports of gunmen also killed — five per RFE/RL, three per one other outlet.
items.html: Iranian state media said Brigadier General Hossein Zarifi, commander of a Revolutionary Guards operational base in Saravan, in Sistan-Baluchestan province on the Pakistani border, was killed Wednesday in clashes with armed men, with reports of gunmen also killed — five per RFE/RL, three per one other outlet. The IRGC described the group as "terrorists" who intended an assassination; the Baloch rights group Haalvsh reported heavy fighting still under way early Thursday. The province has seen a long-running insurgency, and the pro-government Sunni cleric Yousef Gorgij was assassinated in Zahedan on 09-14. (The National, RFE/RL live blog)

items.title: Iranian Revolutionary Guard advisers were in the field helping direct the Houthi offensive that seized Yemen's Red Sea coast in less than 48 hours, ten officials and soldiers told the Associated Press, calling it Iran's most direct intervention on the group's behalf since Yemen's civil war began in 2014.
items.html: Iranian Revolutionary Guard advisers were in the field helping direct the Houthi offensive that seized Yemen's Red Sea coast in less than 48 hours, ten officials and soldiers told the Associated Press, calling it Iran's most direct intervention on the group's behalf since Yemen's civil war began in 2014.
