items.title: Saudi Arabia's Red Sea export hub Yanbu had still not resumed crude tanker loadings on Thursday, two days after the East-West pipeline restarted, and a return to full capacity could take six weeks or more, Reuters reported.
items.html: Saudi Arabia's Red Sea export hub Yanbu had still not resumed crude tanker loadings on Thursday, two days after the East-West pipeline restarted, and a return to full capacity could take six weeks or more, Reuters reported. Crude was flowing into refineries on the Red Sea coast and volumes were building in the pipeline, which three sources said restarted on Tuesday after the 09-11 drone attacks damaged three pumping stations; Aramco told European refiners it is still building a "critical mass" of volumes before it resumes deliveries. Kpler data showed about six tankers due to load at Yanbu from 09-24 to 09-27 and two due on 09-23 that did not load; the line had carried about 4 million barrels a day, roughly 4% of global supply. OilPrice, citing Reuters, said quoted war-risk insurance for Saudi-linked tankers at Yanbu has tripled to about 3% of vessel value from under 1% in early July, against up to 7% at Jizan and 6% to 9% for Hormuz voyages, or roughly $3 million per Yanbu voyage against at least $100,000 before the war. (Reuters via Baird Maritime, Reuters via Devdiscourse, OilPrice via Yahoo Finance)

interpretation.mechanism: Saudi Arabia's Hormuz workaround only helps the oil market if crude actually reaches tankers at Yanbu, and a pipeline that is pumping but not loading leaves the barrels stranded while war-risk insurance at 3% of vessel value makes each Red Sea voyage cost millions, so the bypass supplies less than its nominal 4 million barrels a day and keeps a supply premium in Brent.

scenarios.direction: Loadings restart within days as Aramco builds volumes, and Brent gives back part of Thursday's supply premium.
scenarios.why: Kpler shows about six tankers scheduled to load from 09-24 to 09-27 and Aramco says it needs days to build volumes and finish pressure tests.
scenarios.precedent: 09-21: Reuters reported Saudi crude flows partially recovering as Gulf loadings increased, the last time exports improved after the 09-11 shutdown.

scenarios.direction: A further Houthi strike near Yanbu or Taif or a slower repair keeps loadings halted, and Brent tests Thursday's $108 high.
scenarios.why: Saudi forces intercepted six Houthi missiles aimed at Taif and Yanbu on Thursday, and it may take six weeks or more for the line to return to full capacity.
scenarios.precedent: 09-11: drone attacks shut the pipeline and stopped loadings, and Brent jumped nearly $3 in the following sessions (Reuters, 09-15).

interpretation.context_note: capital-context.yaml's conflict_risk_premium (asof 08-25) predates the 09-11 pipeline attack, so it is used for logic only. Loading status is from Reuters' industry sources and Kpler schedules, not Aramco, which did not immediately comment; insurance figures are OilPrice's summary of Reuters.

items.title: Saudi Aramco chief executive Amin Nasser said Thursday that any disruption to its operations can be fixed "within days" and that Aramco is studying a fourth and a fifth crude export route and more storage abroad, including in Japan.
items.html: Saudi Aramco chief executive Amin Nasser said Thursday that any disruption to its operations can be fixed "within days" and that Aramco is studying a fourth and a fifth crude export route and more storage abroad, including in Japan. Speaking to Nikkei Asia in Tokyo, Nasser said Aramco has three main routes and can also use the 320km Sumed pipeline that carries Red Sea crude to the Mediterranean through Egypt, that "we never stopped" supplying customers, and that barrels offered outside existing sales agreements will not return to the market "until the situation improves"; he cited the 2019 drone attack, after which operations were fully restored in 11 days, and said Aramco is in talks with Japanese authorities and partners on storage there. (Asharq Al-Awsat, Saudi Gazette)

items.title: Hedge funds' leveraged Treasury basis trades have shrunk about 20% this year to roughly $1.2 trillion, Morgan Stanley estimates, removing some of the borrowed-money amplification that worsened past bond selloffs.
items.html: Hedge funds' leveraged Treasury basis trades have shrunk about 20% this year to roughly $1.2 trillion, Morgan Stanley estimates, removing some of the borrowed-money amplification that worsened past bond selloffs. A Reuters analysis attributes the pullback to lower profits rather than forced selling: a mostly orderly rise in rate expectations, softer asset-manager demand for Treasury futures, higher Treasury inventories at big dealer banks after a rule change, and Treasury's buybacks, which have lifted prices of older off-the-run bonds and squeezed the trade's gains. Bank of America's Meghan Swiber says the opportunity set is simply smaller; the retreat so far is concentrated in 2-year and 5-year futures. Whether the buyback is what tipped it is Reuters' framing of one contributing factor among several, not a finding. (Reuters via Kitco, Reuters)

items.title: France's 10-year borrowing cost rose to a new 18-year high of about 4.7% on Thursday, more than a full percentage point above Germany's, as strategists warned the 2027 budget fight could topple the government.
items.html: France's 10-year borrowing cost rose to a new 18-year high of about 4.7% on Thursday, more than a full percentage point above Germany's, as strategists warned the 2027 budget fight could topple the government. CNBC saw the 10-year OAT at 4.6696%, and TradingView reported the 4.7% high as elevated oil and strong data, including euro-zone private-sector activity growing at its fastest pace in nearly three and a half years on Wednesday, reinforced bets on further European Central Bank tightening, with money markets pricing at least one more hike by year-end. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu's draft 2027 budget, with about €54bn of spending cuts, goes to parliament in early October ahead of a November 17 vote; France projects debt at 119.3% of GDP in 2026, and HSBC noted that non-domestic holders now own more than half of OATs. Eurasia Group's Mujtaba Rahman said in a Monday note that a tough draft "risks toppling the government." (CNBC, TradingView)

interpretation.mechanism: A fractured parliament, a tough 2027 budget and a rising ECB rate path raise France's risk premium: the OAT-Bund gap above 100bp, with more than half the debt held by foreign investors who may be less sticky, is being priced before the budget even reaches parliament, and the ECB is unlikely to buy bonds unless markets turn disorderly.

scenarios.direction: The OAT-Bund spread widens toward the top of ING's 100-125bp range as the draft budget goes to parliament in early October and a no-confidence vote before the 11-17 budget vote becomes plausible.
scenarios.why: Opposition to the pension freeze and spending cuts is broad, and Eurasia Group says a tough draft risks toppling the government.
scenarios.precedent: 09-18: France's premium over Germany passed 100bp for the first time since the 2012 euro crisis, up from about half that before the 2024 snap election (The Cross-Border Rate Leg 09-18 entry).

scenarios.direction: Lecornu forces the budget through with constitutional powers or a compromise, and the spread stabilises near 100bp.
scenarios.why: Pre-election caution makes a government collapse costly for every faction, and Lecornu has used the clause before.
scenarios.precedent: Lecornu did not pass the 2026 budget until February this year, using a constitutional clause that bypasses parliament (CNBC).

interpretation.context_note: capital-context.yaml has no France reading; this uses the map's own cross-border-rates thread and CNBC's 09-24 read. OAT levels are Thursday intraday reads.

items.title: The UK 10-year gilt yield rose to 5.38% by mid-morning Thursday, close to last week's 19-year high, adding pressure on Chancellor John Healey's budget next month.
items.html: The UK 10-year gilt yield rose to 5.38% by mid-morning Thursday, close to last week's 19-year high, adding pressure on Chancellor John Healey's budget next month. Analysts say recent rises have wiped out more than half of the £24bn of headroom against Labour's fiscal rules, and Bank of England chief economist Clare Lombardelli said in Warsaw that policy "is increasingly likely to need to tighten if elevated energy prices persist, absent clear evidence of disinflation or weaker activity." By the London close CNBC's tracker had the 10-year gilt at 5.371%, slightly lower on the day after a 5.397% high, and the Telegraph put the 30-year gilt at 5.87%, near its highest since 1998. (The Guardian)

items.title: Germany's 10-year Bund yield reached 3.57% on Thursday, its highest since June 2009, as Berlin's finance agency said it expects record borrowing this year and more next.
items.html: Germany's 10-year Bund yield reached 3.57% on Thursday, its highest since June 2009, as Berlin's finance agency said it expects record borrowing this year and more next. The Telegraph's live blog said demand from traditional buyers such as pension funds is declining while defence spending lifts issuance; CNBC's tracker had the Bund at 3.598% at the European close after a 3.615% day high, and the 10-year OAT at 4.657% (-5.7 basis points on the day) after a 4.719% high, so European yields eased into the close while US yields kept rising. (The Telegraph live blog via Yahoo Finance, CNBC)

items.title: Italy's government turned on its statistics bureau ISTAT after the bureau confirmed on Tuesday that the 2025 budget deficit was 3.1% of GDP, just above the EU's 3% limit, leaving Rome in the bloc's excessive-deficit procedure.
items.html: Italy's government turned on its statistics bureau ISTAT after the bureau confirmed on Tuesday that the 2025 budget deficit was 3.1% of GDP, just above the EU's 3% limit, leaving Rome in the bloc's excessive-deficit procedure. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, who faces a national election next year, said "I don't know whether ISTAT is underestimating Italians or the government's performance", and Economy Minister Giancarlo Giorgetti said its compilation method was "not always compatible with the needs of public accounts"; ISTAT declined to comment on Meloni's remarks, a source there said it follows European Statistical System methods, and a former director called the attacks a scapegoating of an independent institution. Reuters reported the dispute Thursday. (Reuters via Devdiscourse)

items.title: China's Commerce Ministry confirmed Thursday that the two countries held their first talks on artificial intelligence and that senior negotiators also discussed plans to reduce tariffs and extend their trade arrangements, hours before Xi and Trump were due to meet at the White House.
items.html: China's Commerce Ministry confirmed Thursday that the two countries held their first talks on artificial intelligence and that senior negotiators also discussed plans to reduce tariffs and extend their trade arrangements, hours before Xi and Trump were due to meet at the White House. Vice Premier He Lifeng and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent met in New York beforehand; the ministry called the talks constructive and said they reached multiple points of consensus. Trump posted that "Super Intelligence (SI) will be a big topic of discussion, but I want to leave it exactly where it is. That is China's position also. Our guardrail is the DOJ!" The arrival ceremony, Rose Garden military review, bilateral meeting and state dinner were still to come at the time of writing, so no summit outcome, and no market reaction to one, existed yet; Bessent's Wednesday statement that the truce is extended to January 10 is in the 09-23 digest. (CNBC, CNBC on the summit schedule)

items.title: Trump and Xi opened their White House summit Thursday with warm public remarks and no announced trade, tariff or chip agreement by about 2:35pm ET, and the extension of the US-China trade truce to January 10 still rests on Treasury Secretary Bessent's Wednesday statement rather than a joint text.
items.html: Trump and Xi opened their White House summit Thursday with warm public remarks and no announced trade, tariff or chip agreement by about 2:35pm ET, and the extension of the US-China trade truce to January 10 still rests on Treasury Secretary Bessent's Wednesday statement rather than a joint text. Trump cited "tremendous strides" on trade including new market access for farmers, and Xi called for "candid, in-depth and continued dialogue", regular military-to-military communication and AI development kept "under human control"; Bessent said Wednesday the truce conditions stay in effect until January 10, 2027 and that he was unsure a "bigger deal" could be reached by then or whether the truce would be extended again. As of Supply Chain Dive's Thursday morning report the White House had not documented the extension, China's Foreign Ministry declined to confirm it, and the Commerce Ministry said only that negotiators discussed extending the arrangements. Reuters described the summit as expected to be heavy on symbolism and light on substance, and the indexes moved with oil and yields rather than summit headlines through mid-afternoon; the state dinner is tonight. (Yonhap, The Guardian, Supply Chain Dive via Yahoo Finance, China Foreign Ministry briefing)

urls.label: Supply Chain Dive via Yahoo Finance

items.title: Oracle sent the Blue Owl-owned developer of its Project Jupiter data center in New Mexico a force majeure notice, Bloomberg reported Thursday, seeking to put off payments if the 2.45-gigawatt Stargate campus fails to come online in 2028 as planned.
items.html: Oracle sent the Blue Owl-owned developer of its Project Jupiter data center in New Mexico a force majeure notice, Bloomberg reported Thursday, seeking to put off payments if the 2.45-gigawatt Stargate campus fails to come online in 2028 as planned. Oracle says the project "remains on our planned schedule" and it is "fully committed to New Mexico"; Blue Owl said the notice "does not change the financial commitments to this multi-year project." Bloomberg says Oracle is not trying to walk away as the site's main tenant, that it is "not certain" the maneuver would free Oracle from its agreed obligations, and that the notice could alarm the roughly 20 banks behind an $18bn loan that, according to one person, trades below 90 cents on the dollar. The developer is Stack Infrastructure, a Blue Owl portfolio company; the campus's gas pipeline has already slipped to February 2027 after state land-office denials, and on Oracle's 09-10 earnings call co-CEO Clay Magouyrk said Jupiter would not affect fiscal 2027 guidance (CNBC). Oracle shares fell about 4% to 6% in morning trading, Blue Owl about 4% to 5% and Bloom Energy about 6%. By about 2:35pm ET Reuters had Oracle down 4.1% and Blue Owl down 5%, and at 3:10pm CNBC's quotes had Oracle at $139.42 (-3.6%, after a $133.48 low) and Blue Owl at $9.14 (-4.8%). (Bloomberg, Bloomberg via Yahoo Finance, CNBC)

interpretation.mechanism: Lease-backed data-center debt is repaid from the anchor tenant's contracted payments, so a force majeure notice from that tenant, even a precautionary one, puts the cash flow behind the $18bn bank loan in doubt and hits the loan's price, which is already below 90 cents and prices how banks treat the next Stargate-scale lease.

scenarios.direction: The Project Jupiter loan slides further and lenders demand tighter terms on other lease-backed AI data-center debt.
scenarios.why: Bloomberg says the notice could alarm the roughly 20 lending banks, and the loan was already stressed before it.
scenarios.precedent: 09-18: the $18bn Project Jupiter loan stalled in syndication at 89 to 91 cents on the dollar, and on 09-22 the Jane Street-leased Oklahoma bond traded at 11.3% against 8.9% at issue.

scenarios.direction: Oracle and Blue Owl both restate their commitments, the notice reads as a protective legal step, and the loan stabilises near its current price.
scenarios.why: Oracle says it is fully committed and Blue Owl says the notice does not change its financial commitments.

interpretation.context_note: Bloomberg's own caveat is that it is not certain the maneuver would free Oracle from its obligations, and it says Oracle is seeking to defer payments rather than walk away as the main tenant; the loan price is one unnamed source's figure, and the developer (Blue Owl's Stack Infrastructure) is separately reported to be facing a delayed gas pipeline.

items.title: Oracle's credit default swaps hit a record high on Thursday and the yield on its 6.7% bonds due 2056 crossed 8% for the first time, Seeking Alpha reported, citing Zerohedge.
items.html: Oracle's credit default swaps hit a record high on Thursday and the yield on its 6.7% bonds due 2056 crossed 8% for the first time, Seeking Alpha reported, citing Zerohedge. Seeking Alpha said the cost of insuring Oracle's debt reached unprecedented levels on the day of Bloomberg's force majeure report, that the 2056 yield now sits above a 7.5% average for B2/B-rated bonds although Oracle is rated Baa2/BBB-, and, per Zerohedge, that a downgrade to junk would remove about $120bn of its bonds from investment-grade indexes; the article gave no CDS level, and Oracle's five-year CDS had already reached about 2.03 percentage points in July, then an 18-year high (Bloomberg, ICE Data Services). Blue Owl, whose Stack unit developed Jupiter, was down about 4% near $9.18 at 3:39pm ET and about 47% over the past year; Oracle was at $139.21 (-3.7%) after a $133.48 low. (Seeking Alpha, 24/7 Wall St. via Yahoo Finance)

interpretation.mechanism: Oracle funds a buildout that outruns its free cash flow with debt and equity, so what lenders charge to hold or insure its paper sets its cost of capital directly. A record credit default swap price and an 8% yield on a Baa2/BBB- bond mean the market is pricing some chance of a downgrade toward junk, which matters because index rules would force sales of bonds that investment-grade funds must hold, and a higher funding cost for Oracle flows into how banks and private lenders price the next Stargate-scale lease.

scenarios.direction: The credit measures keep widening and Oracle's next debt or equity raise costs visibly more, tightening terms across lender-financed AI data-center projects.
scenarios.why: The force majeure notice arrives while the $18bn Project Jupiter loan already trades below 90 cents on the dollar (Bloomberg) and Oracle told investors on 09-10 that several planned sites were not delivered in the first quarter.
scenarios.precedent: 07-20: Oracle's five-year credit default swaps reached about 2.03 percentage points, an 18-year high (Bloomberg, ICE Data Services), and this week's record is a further step on the same path.

scenarios.direction: Oracle's statements that Jupiter is on schedule and its $664bn backlog hold, and the credit measures stabilise once the notice is read as a contractual protection rather than a retreat.
scenarios.why: Oracle and Blue Owl both say the notice does not change their commitments, and Bloomberg says Oracle is not trying to walk away.

interpretation.context_note: The record and the 8% yield are Zerohedge's figures as relayed by Seeking Alpha, which gave no CDS level, so treat the magnitude as unconfirmed; capital-context.yaml (asof 08-25) has no Oracle credit reading and is used for the reaction-function logic only. Prices for Oracle and Blue Owl are intraday reads from CNBC's quote feed at 3:39pm ET.

items.title: U.S. Rep. Teresa Leger Fernández called Thursday for a "pause" on data centers in New Mexico and published "No Blank Checks for Data Centers" standards, on the day Bloomberg reported Oracle's force majeure notice on Project Jupiter.
items.html: U.S. Rep. Teresa Leger Fernández called Thursday for a "pause" on data centers in New Mexico and published "No Blank Checks for Data Centers" standards, on the day Bloomberg reported Oracle's force majeure notice on Project Jupiter. Source NM said the standards require a data center to show it will not raise electricity bills or harm water resources, meet the state's renewable-energy requirements, create well-paid union jobs, take no taxpayer subsidies and win community approval; state lawmakers are preparing to consider a moratorium next session, Democratic gubernatorial candidate Deb Haaland says she would sign a moratorium order on her first day, and the State Ethics Commission reported last week that Oracle spent more than $3.4 million on advertising aimed at influencing Jupiter's air-permit process. (Source NM)

items.title: JPMorgan upgraded CoreWeave to overweight from neutral on Thursday, arguing the AI cloud provider has pricing power as customers pay up for scarce compute and for short-term contracts.
items.html: JPMorgan upgraded CoreWeave to overweight from neutral on Thursday, arguing the AI cloud provider has pricing power as customers pay up for scarce compute and for short-term contracts. Analyst Samik Chatterjee cited a roughly 25% price increase across CoreWeave's SKUs in July, contracts signed in its fiscal third quarter at about $40 million per megawatt, and management's indication that newer contracts carry 5 to 10 percentage points more contribution margin; the call comes ahead of the company's customer conference next week and follows UBS's Buy call. The shares were roughly flat in the morning, with 24/7 Wall St. noting a muted reaction given capital intensity, debt and an at-the-market share offering, but were up 3.9% at $90.30 by 3:10pm ET on CNBC's quote. (Investor's Business Daily, Benzinga)

items.title: BNP Paribas Exane upgraded Nebius to Outperform from Neutral and raised its price target to $399 from $260 on Thursday, and the AI cloud provider's shares rose about 9% to $246.87 by 3:13pm ET.
items.html: BNP Paribas Exane upgraded Nebius to Outperform from Neutral and raised its price target to $399 from $260 on Thursday, and the AI cloud provider's shares rose about 9% to $246.87 by 3:13pm ET. Nebius has announced that prices for selected Nvidia GPU instances rise roughly 17% to 21% on October 1, and about 25% for some AMD EPYC CPU services, its second price increase in three months according to 24/7 Wall St.; the move fed the same compute-pricing-power argument JPMorgan made for CoreWeave, though the target range among analysts still spans $84 to $410. Bank of America also raised its revenue estimates for 2026 through 2028 on Thursday, reiterating Buy with a $310 target; analyst Tal Liani said Nebius uses long-duration hyperscaler contracts for a stable base while reserving capacity for one- to three-year contracts priced at roughly twice hyperscaler rates. (GuruFocus via Yahoo Finance, 24/7 Wall St. via Yahoo Finance, CNBC midday movers)

items.title: SoftBank's stake in OpenAI will reach about 13% of its equity once the $10 billion third tranche of its $30 billion 2026 commitment closes, due next week, Reuters said in a factbox on the day SoftBank priced its record $11.1bn bond sale.
items.html: SoftBank's stake in OpenAI will reach about 13% of its equity once the $10 billion third tranche of its $30 billion 2026 commitment closes, due next week, Reuters said in a factbox on the day SoftBank priced its record $11.1bn bond sale. SoftBank first put $500 million into OpenAI in 2024, about $30bn more in 2025 and committed $30bn in 2026; rising OpenAI valuations had produced $45bn of unrealised gains by the end of June, but OpenAI has delayed its own listing, which holds up SoftBank's ability to realise them. SoftBank's shares jumped more than 7% when Tokyo reopened Thursday after a three-day holiday, CNBC reported. (Reuters via Global Banking & Finance, SoftBank Group release, CNBC)

items.title: A consortium backed by BlackRock and IFM Investors is in exclusive talks to buy Stack Infrastructure's Asia-Pacific data-center portfolio for up to $25 billion, Bloomberg reported Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter.
items.html: A consortium backed by BlackRock and IFM Investors is in exclusive talks to buy Stack Infrastructure's Asia-Pacific data-center portfolio for up to $25 billion, Bloomberg reported Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter. The group includes the BlackRock-backed AI Infrastructure Partnership, is preparing due diligence and hopes to agree terms soon with Stack's owner, Blue Owl Capital; Bloomberg reported in May that Stack was weighing a sale of its Asia operations at more than $30 billion. Reuters could not immediately verify the report, and talks could be prolonged or fail. Stack operates in Tokyo, Osaka, Sydney and Melbourne. (Economic Times, from Reuters)

items.title: Saudi Arabia's Humain, owned by the Public Investment Fund, awarded infrastructure works for a planned 6-gigawatt hyperscale AI data-centre campus in east Riyadh to Dammam-based Al-Yamama, MEED reported Thursday.
items.html: Saudi Arabia's Humain, owned by the Public Investment Fund, awarded infrastructure works for a planned 6-gigawatt hyperscale AI data-centre campus in east Riyadh to Dammam-based Al-Yamama, MEED reported Thursday. The 24-square-kilometre Al-Saad site is to be built in two phases across six 1GW plots on an early-contractor-involvement basis, with a 2,000MVA bulk supply point, two substations of 500MVA and 200MVA, and water, sewage and fibre networks; Humain tendered the work in May, and Hatch, Egis and JLL advise it. (MEED)

items.title: A paper for Brookings' fall economics conference projects that AI investment will total $10.3 trillion from 2025 to 2032, an average 3.63% of US GDP a year and more than the canal, railroad, highway or telecom booms, and says the financing has shifted into off-balance-sheet vehicles that make correlated exposures "hard to observe before a downturn."
items.html: A paper for Brookings' fall economics conference projects that AI investment will total $10.3 trillion from 2025 to 2032, an average 3.63% of US GDP a year and more than the canal, railroad, highway or telecom booms, and says the financing has shifted into off-balance-sheet vehicles that make correlated exposures "hard to observe before a downturn." Columbia's Stijn Van Nieuwerburgh counts about 183 gigawatts of new data-centre capacity against 57 installed today and calculates the industry would need about $3.7tn of annual revenue by 2032, roughly 80% yearly growth from the $100bn that OpenAI and Anthropic earn combined; he told reporters the opacity of the special-purpose vehicles is "reminiscent of what happened in the subprime mortgage crisis," while the paper itself says it is premature to call the risk systemic. Brookings posted the summary Wednesday and the paper is presented Friday. (Brookings, Reuters via SRN News)

items.title: About 328 million SpaceX shares came out of post-IPO lockup on Thursday, roughly $48.7bn at Wednesday's $148.36 close, with further tranches due October 9 and October 24; the stock was down about 1% at $146.95 at 3:39pm ET.
items.html: About 328 million SpaceX shares came out of post-IPO lockup on Thursday, roughly $48.7bn at Wednesday's $148.36 close, with further tranches due October 9 and October 24; the stock was down about 1% at $146.95 at 3:39pm ET. Stocktwits said the release follows 911.5 million shares on August 6 and 319 million on August 20, and that becoming eligible does not mean holders will sell; Mizuho reiterated Outperform with a $200 target, an SEC filing dated 09-22 showed President Gwynne Shotwell proposed selling 342,170 shares worth about $52 million, and Starship Flight 14 is targeted for September 28. (Stocktwits via Yahoo Finance)

items.title: Moody's revised its outlook on Baidu to negative from stable on Thursday, affirming the A3 rating, as heavy AI spending weighs on cash flow and leverage.
items.html: Moody's revised its outlook on Baidu to negative from stable on Thursday, affirming the A3 rating, as heavy AI spending weighs on cash flow and leverage. Baidu's capital spending rose to RMB17 billion in the first half of 2026 from RMB7 billion a year earlier, free cash flow turned negative, adjusted debt reached RMB113 billion and adjusted debt-to-EBITDA rose to 3.3 times from 2.5 times at the end of 2025; Moody's expects 3.3 to 3.5 times over the next 12 to 18 months but says RMB166 billion of cash and short-term investments against RMB34 billion of near-term maturities gives ample liquidity. AI-powered initiatives grew 37% and are now more than half of general revenue, while search revenue fell 26%. (Investing.com via Yahoo Finance Australia)

items.title: OpenEvidence, the clinical AI search company, raised $250 million from hospital systems and Andreessen Horowitz at a $15 billion valuation, Business Insider reported Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter.
items.html: OpenEvidence, the clinical AI search company, raised $250 million from hospital systems and Andreessen Horowitz at a $15 billion valuation, Business Insider reported Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter. The valuation is up from $12 billion in January; the company has raised more than $1 billion in the past year, Business Insider said it could be open to an acquisition that includes access to compute, which it could not verify, and Anthropic announced a partnership with it this week. (Business Insider)

items.title: CDC Data Centres, part-owned by Australia's Future Fund and Infratil, is pitching a A$15 billion (US$10.5bn), 1.4-gigawatt data-centre campus near Wagga Wagga in New South Wales, according to a scoping report lodged with the state on September 16.
items.html: CDC Data Centres, part-owned by Australia's Future Fund and Infratil, is pitching a A$15 billion (US$10.5bn), 1.4-gigawatt data-centre campus near Wagga Wagga in New South Wales, according to a scoping report lodged with the state on September 16. Mingtiandi, reporting it Thursday, said the campus on 103.8 hectares of grazing land at Gregadoo would be the largest planned in the state and is pitched as sovereign computing for government, defence and AI workloads, echoing Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's July 15 speech on AI and national security. (Mingtiandi)

items.title: Xi told Trump he hopes the US will "uphold the correct position of opposing 'Taiwan independence'" and handle the Taiwan question "with prudence," according to the Chinese state news agency Xinhua's readout of their Oval Office talks; the White House had issued no readout of its own by about 3pm ET.
items.html: Xi told Trump he hopes the US will "uphold the correct position of opposing 'Taiwan independence'" and handle the Taiwan question "with prudence," according to the Chinese state news agency Xinhua's readout of their Oval Office talks; the White House had issued no readout of its own by about 3pm ET. The bilateral began about 11:45am ET, ran about 90 minutes and was closed to the press pool, and Trump waved off shouted questions on whether Taiwan, AI or the jailed Hong Kong publisher Jimmy Lai came up, saying only "great meeting." Congress has approved a multi-billion-dollar Taiwan arms sale that awaits Trump's signature (BBC), and after his May Beijing visit Trump said he was suspending a package worth about $14 billion, calling it a "very good negotiating chip" (Guardian, citing AP); the US position is that it does not support Taiwan independence (CNN). (CNN live updates, BBC live page)

items.title: Xi told Trump China supports the US and Iran returning to the 14-point memorandum of understanding reached in June and hopes they resume negotiations as soon as possible and ultimately reach a nuclear agreement, Xinhua reported; Al Jazeera adds that Chinese state media said he also backs an end to naval blockades.
items.html: Xi told Trump China supports the US and Iran returning to the 14-point memorandum of understanding reached in June and hopes they resume negotiations as soon as possible and ultimately reach a nuclear agreement, Xinhua reported; Al Jazeera adds that Chinese state media said he also backs an end to naval blockades. This is the Chinese account; no US account of the Iran discussion had been published by about 3pm. AP notes China has so far resisted US urging to press Iran to accept US terms to end the nearly seven-month war. (Guardian live blog, Al Jazeera live blog, Associated Press)

items.title: At the White House welcome Xi said China and the US "will both lose in confrontation," called for regular military-to-military dialogue and crisis-communication mechanisms so the "Thucydides trap can be overcome," and invited 100,000 young Americans to study in China over five years, while Trump called their relationship a "truly great friendship" and said they had made "tremendous strides."
items.html: At the White House welcome Xi said China and the US "will both lose in confrontation," called for regular military-to-military dialogue and crisis-communication mechanisms so the "Thucydides trap can be overcome," and invited 100,000 young Americans to study in China over five years, while Trump called their relationship a "truly great friendship" and said they had made "tremendous strides." Xi also announced two giant pandas will go to Zoo Atlanta. On AI, Xi said development must be "always under human control"; Trump wrote that he wants to "leave it exactly where it is. That is China's position also," and AP says the US had proposed an AI-incident "notification mechanism" at the finance ministers' meeting earlier in the week. A black-tie state dinner with Bezos, Pichai, Altman, Cook, Musk, Zuckerberg and Huang expected follows this evening. (BBC live page, Guardian live blog, Associated Press)

items.title: China's Commerce Ministry said Thursday that US and Chinese trade negotiators held their first talks focused specifically on artificial intelligence and reached consensus on several issues, a day after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the trade truce had been extended to January 10.
items.html: China's Commerce Ministry said Thursday that US and Chinese trade negotiators held their first talks focused specifically on artificial intelligence and reached consensus on several issues, a day after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the trade truce had been extended to January 10. Spokesman He Yadong said tariff reductions and continuing the arrangements from last October's Kuala Lumpur meetings were also discussed; the coverage read did not include a Chinese statement giving the January 10 date, and Bessent said Beijing might make further announcements in coming days, such as farm purchases and opening parts of financial services. (Quartz, citing CNBC and NBC)

items.title: Ethiopia's army said Thursday it had repelled attacks by Tigrayan forces and their allies in the north, its first statement since fighting began on Wednesday, saying hostilities started in an area of Amhara region close to the Tigray border and that its soldiers inflicted heavy casualties and seized weapons.
items.html: Ethiopia's army said Thursday it had repelled attacks by Tigrayan forces and their allies in the north, its first statement since fighting began on Wednesday, saying hostilities started in an area of Amhara region close to the Tigray border and that its soldiers inflicted heavy casualties and seized weapons. The Tigray People's Liberation Front had not commented and the BBC could not verify the army's claims or report from Tigray; a Mekelle resident told the BBC the city itself was calm, with no clashes, though people were short of cash and expecting communications to be cut. Ethiopian Airlines has cancelled all flights to Tigray. (BBC News)

items.title: Tigray's vice-president Amanuel Assefa told AFP on Thursday "we are in the situation of full-blown war now," as a humanitarian source in Afar reported heavy artillery attacks by Tigrayan forces on the town of Yallo, near the Tigray border.
items.html: Tigray's vice-president Amanuel Assefa told AFP on Thursday "we are in the situation of full-blown war now," as a humanitarian source in Afar reported heavy artillery attacks by Tigrayan forces on the town of Yallo, near the Tigray border. The claim comes from one side of the conflict and AFP's account of the Afar fighting rests on a single humanitarian source; the BBC repeats both. The EU and IGAD have called for immediate de-escalation. (AFP, Al Jazeera)

items.title: ACLED reported that armed clashes continued on Thursday along the Tigray-Afar border and in Amhara's Wag Hemra and North Wello zones, where federal troops, Amhara riot police and local militia are fighting Fano fighters and Tigray's forces, and that a new front reportedly opened in western Tigray near the Tekeze River.
items.html: ACLED reported that armed clashes continued on Thursday along the Tigray-Afar border and in Amhara's Wag Hemra and North Wello zones, where federal troops, Amhara riot police and local militia are fighting Fano fighters and Tigray's forces, and that a new front reportedly opened in western Tigray near the Tekeze River. ACLED's local sources also reported that the head of the Tigray Police Force and a senior TPLF member defected on 09-23 (the text read does not say to whom) and rumoured that a senior Tigrayan general had been suspended; ACLED noted that the airport seizures are not in themselves militarily decisive but that in 2019 and 2020 action by one group prompted others to act, and the new alliance includes those groups. Human Rights Watch said the fighting erupted on 09-22 after clashes and airstrikes since August. (ACLED, Human Rights Watch)

items.title: Ethiopia's army said Thursday afternoon that a counter-offensive in North Wollo, in Amhara region, had killed at least 272 Tigrayan fighters and wounded about 260, and flights to the UNESCO-listed town of Lalibela were suspended as AFP received reports of fighting nearby.
items.html: Ethiopia's army said Thursday afternoon that a counter-offensive in North Wollo, in Amhara region, had killed at least 272 Tigrayan fighters and wounded about 260, and flights to the UNESCO-listed town of Lalibela were suspended as AFP received reports of fighting nearby. The figures come from the Ethiopian National Defence Force's Facebook statement and could not be independently verified; DW notes there was no breakdown between soldiers and civilians. The US ambassador in Addis Ababa, Ervin Massinga, said he was "disappointed" the TPLF, which the US sanctioned earlier this year, had launched a large-scale offensive and rejected African Union-sponsored dialogue, and TPLF vice-president Amanuel Assefa told AFP the Tigrayan side has not asked for Eritrean intervention "not yet". (Al Jazeera, DW)

items.title: Yahya Rahim Safavi, a senior adviser to Iran's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei, warned Thursday that Iran may expand the war to the Indian Ocean if the US or Israel attacks again, saying that since the conflict has spread from the Persian Gulf and Hormuz to the Red Sea, "the front will expand even further, reaching the Indian Ocean and perhaps beyond."
items.html: Yahya Rahim Safavi, a senior adviser to Iran's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei, warned Thursday that Iran may expand the war to the Indian Ocean if the US or Israel attacks again, saying that since the conflict has spread from the Persian Gulf and Hormuz to the Red Sea, "the front will expand even further, reaching the Indian Ocean and perhaps beyond." He spoke in a video released by the Fars news agency. Kurdistan24 says it is the first reported instance of an adviser to the supreme leader naming the Indian Ocean and notes that the US-British base at Diego Garcia lies there, nearly 4,000 km from Iran; the statement is a threat, not an action, and no attack has been reported. (Kurdistan24, AFP via NAMPA)

items.title: The UAE's General Civil Aviation Authority announced Thursday it was suspending all flights by Iranian airlines to and from the country until further notice, as new US secondary sanctions on Iran's aviation industry took effect, and Iran's Tasnim agency said flights to Oman, Georgia, Azerbaijan and Baghdad were also shut.
items.html: The UAE's General Civil Aviation Authority announced Thursday it was suspending all flights by Iranian airlines to and from the country until further notice, as new US secondary sanctions on Iran's aviation industry took effect, and Iran's Tasnim agency said flights to Oman, Georgia, Azerbaijan and Baghdad were also shut. Iran's Civil Aviation Organization had said all Iranian airline flights to the UAE were cancelled from midnight, and an Iran Airtour flight from Tehran to Dubai was cancelled shortly before departure. A senior Iranian official had threatened on Wednesday to make airports "unusable" in any regional country that abides by the US ban; the Reuters report notes Tehran's airport listed no flights to or from Gulf states on Thursday. (Khaleej Times, Reuters via The Straits Times, Al Jazeera)

items.title: US and Iranian negotiators in New York are exploring a phased path out of the war in which Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz and Washington would lift its economic blockade, Reuters reported Thursday, citing Iranian, regional and Western sources; neither side wants to be first to give up its leverage.
items.html: US and Iranian negotiators in New York are exploring a phased path out of the war in which Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz and Washington would lift its economic blockade, Reuters reported Thursday, citing Iranian, regional and Western sources; neither side wants to be first to give up its leverage. A senior Iranian official said the most plausible route is staged, starting with an end to the blockade and reopening of Hormuz, possibly with access to frozen assets, and Reuters says Trump has said a deal could come after the 3 November midterms. Separately, a group of 80 countries, in a statement read by Bahrain's foreign minister at the UN, called for the "full restoration of navigational rights" in the Gulf, and Gulf News reports Iran has presented a roadmap with a region-wide ceasefire of up to 60 days, though Tehran's IRGC-linked Tasnim agency said the Araghchi-Witkoff-Kushner contact had not been "authorised". (Reuters via RNZ, Gulf News live blog)

items.title: The Senate on Thursday rejected, 49 to 50, a resolution directing Trump to end US military action against Iran, with Republicans Rand Paul, Susan Collins, Lisa Murkowski and Thom Tillis voting yes and Democrat John Fetterman voting no.
items.html: The Senate on Thursday rejected, 49 to 50, a resolution directing Trump to end US military action against Iran, with Republicans Rand Paul, Susan Collins, Lisa Murkowski and Thom Tillis voting yes and Democrat John Fetterman voting no. It was a concurrent resolution, which never goes to the president and is largely symbolic; the same measure passed the House 214-208 in July. NBC reports 19 US service members have died in the war and that 62 percent of registered voters in its poll say it was not worth it. (NBC News)

items.title: Saudi Arabia's air defences intercepted and destroyed six ballistic missiles launched by the Houthis at the cities of Taif and Yanbu on Thursday, the Saudi-led coalition's spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki al-Maliki said, and Saudi Civil Defence issued brief danger alerts for Mecca, Jeddah, Yanbu, Taif and Tabuk that were later lifted.
items.html: Saudi Arabia's air defences intercepted and destroyed six ballistic missiles launched by the Houthis at the cities of Taif and Yanbu on Thursday, the Saudi-led coalition's spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki al-Maliki said, and Saudi Civil Defence issued brief danger alerts for Mecca, Jeddah, Yanbu, Taif and Tabuk that were later lifted. Al-Maliki said Houthi "escalations and violations will be dealt with firmly." Attribution to the Houthis is the coalition's, but Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree later said the group had attacked Saudi military sites in Jazan province and had fired dozens of missiles and drones at Saudi targets (Reuters); the group denied targeting Mecca after an earlier alert on 09-18. (Saudi Gazette, Reuters via The Straits Times, Gulf News live blog, The Week)

items.title: Yemeni government forces said Thursday they repelled coordinated Houthi attacks in Taiz governorate's Wadi al-Maqatirah area on Wednesday night, aimed at reaching positions on a key road linking Aden, Lahj and Taiz, and killed or wounded "dozens" of fighters in clashes in the Al Ahkum area earlier on Wednesday.
items.html: Yemeni government forces said Thursday they repelled coordinated Houthi attacks in Taiz governorate's Wadi al-Maqatirah area on Wednesday night, aimed at reaching positions on a key road linking Aden, Lahj and Taiz, and killed or wounded "dozens" of fighters in clashes in the Al Ahkum area earlier on Wednesday. The account is from the government-aligned forces' spokesman, Colonel Majid al-Nuzaili; there was no immediate Houthi comment. (Al Jazeera)

items.title: France will send "soldiers, radars, and defence systems" to help protect Saudi Arabia's Red Sea oil port of Yanbu after Houthi attacks, President Emmanuel Macron said Thursday in an evening television interview.
items.html: France will send "soldiers, radars, and defence systems" to help protect Saudi Arabia's Red Sea oil port of Yanbu after Houthi attacks, President Emmanuel Macron said Thursday in an evening television interview. Macron gave no timetable or numbers in the AFP report; Yanbu was among the cities Saudi Arabia said it defended against six Houthi missiles on Thursday, and Houthis claimed a strike on Aramco's Yanbu facility on 09-19. (Arab News, citing AFP, Gulf News live blog)

items.title: Denmark's defence intelligence service warned Thursday that Russia will intensify its hybrid war against NATO countries in the coming months, with more frequent attacks with greater consequences and a "low but growing" risk of a limited Russian military attack on a neighbouring NATO country, while calling an outright invasion "highly unlikely" but not excludable.
items.html: Denmark's defence intelligence service warned Thursday that Russia will intensify its hybrid war against NATO countries in the coming months, with more frequent attacks with greater consequences and a "low but growing" risk of a limited Russian military attack on a neighbouring NATO country, while calling an outright invasion "highly unlikely" but not excludable. The assessment says Russia is under more pressure than at any point in the war and that the next few years may look like a "window of opportunity" if Moscow doubts the US response; Denmark's civil security agency raised its threat level for destructive cyber attacks from medium to high, citing "specific planning of sabotage actions against Denmark." NATO's top commander, Alexus Grynkewich, told Reuters "we are all eastern flank countries these days." (Kyiv Independent, Guardian Europe live blog)

items.title: Poland's deputy prime minister Krzysztof Gawkowski said a Wednesday-night fire at a Starlink satellite station in Wola Krobowska, central Poland, was deliberate sabotage designed to disable it and disrupt internet access including for the Ukrainian army, while Prime Minister Donald Tusk said "it looks bad" but that he would not call it sabotage without being certain.
items.html: Poland's deputy prime minister Krzysztof Gawkowski said a Wednesday-night fire at a Starlink satellite station in Wola Krobowska, central Poland, was deliberate sabotage designed to disable it and disrupt internet access including for the Ukrainian army, while Prime Minister Donald Tusk said "it looks bad" but that he would not call it sabotage without being certain. The station, which routes traffic to Ukraine using SpaceX systems, remains operational and the investigation is ongoing; Gawkowski said many indications fit a "new Russian doctrine of attack," and the Kremlin had not commented. (BBC News)

items.title: Poland briefly evacuated two border crossings with Ukraine, at Hrubieszów and Dorohusk, during Russian strikes on western Ukraine on Thursday morning, Tusk said, warning that "autumn and winter could indeed prove critical."
items.html: Poland briefly evacuated two border crossings with Ukraine, at Hrubieszów and Dorohusk, during Russian strikes on western Ukraine on Thursday morning, Tusk said, warning that "autumn and winter could indeed prove critical." The Guardian's Europe live blog also reports Czechia scrambling fighter jets on a "combat air patrol" over Poland overnight. (Guardian Europe live blog)

items.title: A Russian strike on a vegetable-storage farm in Stara Hnylytsia, Kharkiv region, killed at least six people and injured 12 on Thursday morning, regional governor Oleh Syniehubov said; Ukrinform later put the dead at seven.
items.html: A Russian strike on a vegetable-storage farm in Stara Hnylytsia, Kharkiv region, killed at least six people and injured 12 on Thursday morning, regional governor Oleh Syniehubov said; Ukrinform later put the dead at seven. Russia had not commented in the coverage read. (Kyiv Independent, Ukrinform)

items.title: Ukrainian drones hit an oil depot's administrative buildings in Russia's Rostov region and set off a fire at an industrial facility in Krasnodar Krai overnight into Thursday, Russian officials said, and Ukraine's General Staff reported strikes on two Russian radar stations and a drone launch site.
items.html: Ukrainian drones hit an oil depot's administrative buildings in Russia's Rostov region and set off a fire at an industrial facility in Krasnodar Krai overnight into Thursday, Russian officials said, and Ukraine's General Staff reported strikes on two Russian radar stations and a drone launch site. Rostov governor Yuri Slyusar said there was no fire and no injuries at the depot; Krasnodar's emergency headquarters attributed the fire to "falling debris" from drones; Russia's Defence Ministry said 40 Ukrainian drones were shot down overnight. (Meduza, Ukrinform)

items.title: Zelensky said Thursday that the G20 summit in Miami in December could open the way to a trilateral meeting of Ukraine, the US and Russia, calling it "one of the best opportunities proposed by the U.S. side," and that Ukraine would support the format if all parties agree.
items.html: Zelensky said Thursday that the G20 summit in Miami in December could open the way to a trilateral meeting of Ukraine, the US and Russia, calling it "one of the best opportunities proposed by the U.S. side," and that Ukraine would support the format if all parties agree. The remark follows Secretary of State Marco Rubio's Wednesday statement that Washington will invite Vladimir Putin; Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Moscow did not read Zelensky's Wednesday remark that he would come to Moscow "on a missile" as ruling out a visit, and Putin continues to avoid an in-person meeting while Zelensky calls for a neutral location. (Kyiv Independent, Kyiv Independent on the "missile" exchange)

items.title: Zelensky said the Trump administration is pressing three immediate steps to de-escalate the war: a mutual halt to strikes on energy infrastructure, reopening of the Black Sea grain corridor and trilateral US-Russia-Ukraine talks, with Abu Dhabi floated as a venue that Kyiv would accept.
items.html: Zelensky said the Trump administration is pressing three immediate steps to de-escalate the war: a mutual halt to strikes on energy infrastructure, reopening of the Black Sea grain corridor and trilateral US-Russia-Ukraine talks, with Abu Dhabi floated as a venue that Kyiv would accept. Axios, via Meduza, reports that Putin's envoy Kirill Dmitriev is due in New York on Thursday to meet Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner on the proposals; Ukrainian outlet ZN.UA said a Budanov-Witkoff-Dmitriev meeting was being arranged there and Russia denied it. Zelensky said he doubts Putin will negotiate and "could find reasons" to avoid a leaders' meeting. (Meduza, citing Axios)

items.title: Zelensky said Ukraine reached an agreement Thursday on a new shipment of missiles for its US-made Patriot air-defence systems, without saying which country would supply them, how many or when.
items.html: Zelensky said Ukraine reached an agreement Thursday on a new shipment of missiles for its US-made Patriot air-defence systems, without saying which country would supply them, how many or when. He spoke to Ukrainian-community leaders in the US; Ukraine faces a critical shortage of the interceptors, the only weapons able to reliably stop Russian ballistic missiles, and no concrete Patriot decision came out of his Tuesday meeting with Trump. (Kyiv Independent)

items.title: A 31-year-old Ukrainian man killed a priest and wounded four other people, two of them critically, in a knife attack at a Benedictine abbey in Jaroslaw, south-east Poland, on Thursday morning, and was arrested.
items.html: A 31-year-old Ukrainian man killed a priest and wounded four other people, two of them critically, in a knife attack at a Benedictine abbey in Jaroslaw, south-east Poland, on Thursday morning, and was arrested. Prosecutors said he had entered Poland from Germany earlier in the day, was reportedly heading for the nearby border crossing back into Ukraine, and that the motive was unclear; Tusk promised the "full severity" of Polish law, Zelensky called it a "horrific crime", and the town declared mourning until the end of the week. The New York Times says it adds to tension between Poland and Ukraine; no link to the war was reported in the coverage read. (Al Jazeera, Reuters via Yahoo)

items.title: Dozens of delegations walked out of the UN General Assembly hall as Netanyahu took the podium, and he opened by telling those who left they were "moral cowards."
items.html: Dozens of delegations walked out of the UN General Assembly hall as Netanyahu took the podium, and he opened by telling those who left they were "moral cowards." The Palestinian mission had urged members to bring staff and "collectively walk out"; Israel's delegation stood and applauded while others booed and jeered, the Assembly president repeatedly called for order, and a majority of seats were empty afterward. He is not due to meet Trump and was to leave New York within hours of speaking to be home before Sukkot begins at sundown Friday. (Associated Press, CBS News)

items.title: Netanyahu told the General Assembly that attacking Iran "was one of the easiest decisions I've ever had to make," said many leaders of countries whose delegates walked out "even thank us privately for taking out Iran's nukes," and thanked Trump for his "bold leadership."
items.html: Netanyahu told the General Assembly that attacking Iran "was one of the easiest decisions I've ever had to make," said many leaders of countries whose delegates walked out "even thank us privately for taking out Iran's nukes," and thanked Trump for his "bold leadership." The claim about private thanks is his own; he also called Turkey the latest "super-spreader of antisemitic lies" and Erdogan a "tyrant," rejected the genocide charge ("Israel didn't commit genocide. Israel prevented genocide"), attacked New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, and held up a pager to recall the 2024 attack on Hezbollah. (MS NOW, Gulf News live blog)

items.title: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas told the General Assembly in a pre-recorded video that Israeli policies now threaten the "very life and existence" of the Palestinian people, after the US denied him and other senior officials visas for the second year running.
items.html: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas told the General Assembly in a pre-recorded video that Israeli policies now threaten the "very life and existence" of the Palestinian people, after the US denied him and other senior officials visas for the second year running. Abbas, 90, called the visa denial "punitive" and asked what the international community is "waiting for before it acts"; the Israeli delegation's seats stood empty while he spoke. (Gulf News live blog, Associated Press)

items.title: Gaza's Health Ministry said five more Palestinians were killed and 35 injured in the 24 hours to Thursday, taking the toll since the October 2025 ceasefire to 1,408 killed and 4,916 wounded and the overall war toll to 73,928 killed and 175,030 injured.
items.html: Gaza's Health Ministry said five more Palestinians were killed and 35 injured in the 24 hours to Thursday, taking the toll since the October 2025 ceasefire to 1,408 killed and 4,916 wounded and the overall war toll to 73,928 killed and 175,030 injured. The ministry's daily report gave no circumstances for the latest deaths. (Anadolu Agency)

items.title: Hamas spokesman Hazem Qassem said in a Thursday statement that the group is "fully ready to implement the roadmap agreed with the Board of Peace," a day after the Board unveiled its $2.45 billion reconstruction plan, while blaming Israel for obstructing the ceasefire and the roadmap and urging the US and the Board to facilitate the entry of the Palestinian technocratic committee and the international force.
items.html: Hamas spokesman Hazem Qassem said in a Thursday statement that the group is "fully ready to implement the roadmap agreed with the Board of Peace," a day after the Board unveiled its $2.45 billion reconstruction plan, while blaming Israel for obstructing the ceasefire and the roadmap and urging the US and the Board to facilitate the entry of the Palestinian technocratic committee and the international force. The statement did not mention disarmament, which Israel and Board officials say must come before reconstruction advances; Hamas agreed to a plan including disarmament last year but the sides have since traded accusations of violations. (Naharnet, TRT World)

items.title: Israeli forces carried out a large detonation around Bint Jbeil in south Lebanon on Thursday and for a second night in a row in al-Khiam, while artillery shelled Beit Yahoun, Shaqra, Kounine, Hadatha and al-Mansouri overnight and strikes hit Mayfadoun, al-Mansouri, Qantara, Wadi al-Hujair and Wadi Slouqi, Lebanese outlet Naharnet reported.
items.html: Israeli forces carried out a large detonation around Bint Jbeil in south Lebanon on Thursday and for a second night in a row in al-Khiam, while artillery shelled Beit Yahoun, Shaqra, Kounine, Hadatha and al-Mansouri overnight and strikes hit Mayfadoun, al-Mansouri, Qantara, Wadi al-Hujair and Wadi Slouqi, Lebanese outlet Naharnet reported. Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam, in New York, was due to meet Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian later Thursday, al-Jadeed TV reported. The detonation and shelling reports rest on Naharnet's live summary; no Israeli comment was found. (Naharnet)

items.title: Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam told Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in New York that Lebanon "does not want to be a battlefield for regional conflicts or an arena for exchanging messages," and said afterward Beirut seeks a "new chapter" in relations with Tehran.
items.html: Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam told Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in New York that Lebanon "does not want to be a battlefield for regional conflicts or an arena for exchanging messages," and said afterward Beirut seeks a "new chapter" in relations with Tehran. The National calls it a rare face-to-face meeting between senior Lebanese and Iranian leaders; Salam's government has been pressing to disarm Hezbollah, which entered the war in March, and Salam also met Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa at the UN and spoke of a "new page" with Damascus. (The National, Naharnet)

items.title: The UN trade body UNCTAD said Gaza's recovery and reconstruction needs have reached an estimated $71.5 billion and its economy is in the "most severe crisis on record," with more than 90 percent of working-age people unemployed and 92 percent of economic establishments damaged or destroyed.
items.html: The UN trade body UNCTAD said Gaza's recovery and reconstruction needs have reached an estimated $71.5 billion and its economy is in the "most severe crisis on record," with more than 90 percent of working-age people unemployed and 92 percent of economic establishments damaged or destroyed. The report was presented at UNCTAD's 73rd session on Thursday and says the figure is likely to rise; about 1.9 million people, nearly 90 percent of Gaza's population, have been displaced, according to the UN. (Al Jazeera)

items.title: Pakistan said it carried out air and drone strikes on 10 locations in Afghanistan early Thursday that it says were used to store and launch drones, and the Taliban government said four civilians were killed in Kandahar, Paktia and Khost provinces and promised an "appropriate response."
items.html: Pakistan said it carried out air and drone strikes on 10 locations in Afghanistan early Thursday that it says were used to store and launch drones, and the Taliban government said four civilians were killed in Kandahar, Paktia and Khost provinces and promised an "appropriate response." Pakistan's information minister said the operation, codenamed "Ghazab Lil Haq," answered an "unlawful incursion into Pakistan by drones" on Wednesday that he said air defences shot down, and called the strikes "precise, calibrated and proportionate"; the Taliban deny launching drones. A resident told AFP a strike hit the centre of Kandahar, the Taliban leader's home city. The fighting resumed after a suicide bombing at a mosque inside a police compound in Kohat, north-west Pakistan, on 18 September killed at least 31 people according to AFP (an earlier count was 21), reigniting clashes after nearly three months of relative calm; the BBC says it is the second wave of Pakistani air strikes on Afghan territory in a week, that the Taliban promised an "appropriate response" and Pakistan warned any further "provocative act" would be answered, and that the UN mission in Afghanistan counted at least 499 civilians killed in cross-border violence between October 2025 and June 2026. (Al Jazeera, BBC News, Afghanistan International)

items.title: The World Health Organization said Congo is running short of health workers to staff treatment centres in the world's fastest-growing Ebola outbreak, particularly in North Kivu, where cases have surged 73 percent over three weeks, even as cases fell 26 percent in Ituri province and 15 percent in Haut-Uele.
items.html: The World Health Organization said Congo is running short of health workers to staff treatment centres in the world's fastest-growing Ebola outbreak, particularly in North Kivu, where cases have surged 73 percent over three weeks, even as cases fell 26 percent in Ituri province and 15 percent in Haut-Uele. The outbreak has spread to seven provinces, with 7,773 confirmed cases and 3,759 deaths on the latest government figures; WHO's regional emergency director said it "is still not under control" and it is on track to pass the 2014-2016 West Africa outbreak, which killed more than 11,000. The WHO statement was made Wednesday and the AP report ran Thursday afternoon. (Associated Press via New York Post)
items.source: Associated Press via New York Post

urls.label: Associated Press via New York Post

2026-09-21.ai: xAI shipped Grok 4.7 on Monday, after Elon Musk's public ship-date promises for it slipped three times since July, pricing it unchanged from Grok 4.6 and pairing it with what it calls its strongest safeguard stack yet. A United Nations scientific panel told governments not to wait for scientific certainty before installing safeguards against AI agents running out of control, publishing its first thematic brief the same week world leaders gather in New York and Washington prepares to host Xi Jinping, Google confirmed its Gemini models broke into three real companies during a misconfigured security test in May, and Ireland's privacy regulator fined it €403 million over its handling of location data. OpenAI and Anthropic are reportedly close to a deal to stress-test each other's models, and OpenAI set up an independent group of mathematicians to guide how its models' math results are reviewed. Beyond that the day was thin: the antitrust suit over the labs' pacing pledge drew no new filings, and no other major lab announced a new model.
2026-09-21.mental-health: IIT Bombay suspended the professor named in the abetment-of-suicide FIR from his administrative post and apologised for its own earlier account of student Sahil Wakode's death, as Mumbai's Crime Branch took over the investigation.
